The British Museum is extending its opening hours and introducing new measures in an effort to clear severe backlogs and overcrowding at its Bayeux Tapestry exhibition.

Confirming the operational overhaul, a spokesperson for the museum told The Independent: "The response to the Bayeux Tapestry has been extraordinary, and we are delighted by the excitement and interest it has generated.

"We also know that some visitors have faced longer queues than we would have wanted, so we are introducing a series of measures - including an audio guide, clearer signage, additional seating and longer opening hours - to make the experience smoother and give more people the time they need to enjoy the Tapestry."

The swift changes follow widespread visitor frustration over two-hour delays and an incident last week where hundreds of ticket holders were turned away when the venue closed early for a private event.

open image in gallery The British Museum has announced new changes to its Bayeux Tapestry exhibition ( Getty )

The museum has since apologised to affected visitors, confirming that anyone turned away will receive a full refund alongside a priority slot to rebook for a rearranged time.

Starting Monday, an audio guide will offer visitors extra historical detail. Clearer signage will explain the introductory displays and videos setting the scene before visitors reach the main showcase, while additional seating will allow for breaks during the wait.

Details on the extended opening hours are set to be announced shortly. The measures build on earlier interventions inside the gallery, where staff banned photography and introduced recorded messages prompting crowds to keep moving steadily along the one-way route.

Ticket demand for the display has been unprecedented since going on sale in July, with a record 100,000 passes sold on the first day alone. Unsuccessful fans will have two further chances to secure entry when additional ticket batches are released in October and January.

open image in gallery On the first day tickets to view the Tapestry went on sale, 100,000 were sold ( Reuters )

On loan from Normandy, where it has been exhibited since 1983, the masterpiece marks the first time the historic work has returned to England since its creation over 900 years ago.

The exhibition opened on 10 September and is scheduled to run until July 2027.

open image in gallery The Tapestry has moved from France to Britain for the first time in nearly a thousand years ( Reuters )

Standard adult entry costs £27 off-peak and £33 during peak hours – compared to the usual €12 (£10) fee at its home in France– while children under 16 enter free of charge.

The 70-metre-long masterpiece is an embroidery of dyed wool thread on linen cloth rather than a woven tapestry, as its name suggests.

Across 58 narrative scenes, it uses Latin inscriptions alongside detailed needlework to depict the extraordinary events surrounding the 1066 Norman Conquest, culminating in the Battle of Hastings and the end of Anglo-Saxon rule in Britain.

The historic work features roughly 626 human figures, 200 horses, 500 other animals, 37 ships, and depictions of key historical phenomena, including an early record of Halley's Comet.

News.title: Jibulu emerges as England World Cup bolter in Sale defeat of Saracens
News.content:
Could Nathan Jibulu, the Sale Sharks hooker, emerge as a bolter for England’s World Cup squad? With Steve Borthwick, the England head coach, watching from the stands, the 23-year-old produced the kind of “wrecking-ball” performance in this surprise victory for the North West side that suggested he is on course to do so.

After their tame defeat by Bristol Bears in the opening round, few had predicted that Alex Sanderson’s side had much hope against Saracens, who were looking to back up their impressive win at Welford Road last weekend. But Jibulu’s powerhouse display on either side of the ball typified their stout and physical resistance, backed up by a masterly display by George Ford.

Given the age and injury profile of England hookers Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie, who both missed this contest, and the fact that Theo Dan has yet to make a forceful challenge for the position in the national side, Sanderson is in no doubt that Jibulu has the X factor required to break into Borthwick’s squad this season.

“This is the player that any time you watch him play, he impacts – he takes metres either side of the ball – and we knew that he had that in him,” Sanderson said.

“It shows he’s of international class. He nailed his line-outs, on the back of that he was a wrecking ball runner causing havoc around the field.

“This is the person that we knew, this is the player that we knew we had in him. It could be the year where he explodes onto the international scene. I hope it is, but it’s early days.

“He’s that quality, he’s that kind of an athlete. You can get away with being fast and skilful in the Prem, but it’s another level again in terms of the power that’s required at international level. And he’s got that ability, he’s immensely strong.”

Borthwick will have left the StoneX Stadium on Sunday evening with a full notebook. Ben Bamber, Sale’s 6ft 9ins lock, has also been attracting his interest and it was Bamber who crossed for the decisive try, Sale’s third, hitting a great line off Ford to finish like an outside centre.

News.title: Brilliant Hamilton storms to podium despite another Ferrari blunder
News.content:
One of the big talking points heading into the weekend has been the cooling vests drivers wear under their overalls (as opposed to the jacket-like ones they wear when they’re out of their cars). Russell told us in our Brits media session on Thursday that Mercedes had decided to forego the vests here, since the technology was not yet refined. The system works by pumping a coolant through thin tubes stitched into the vest.

Drivers have complained that the connecting valve to the pump, which was originally placed on the side of the vest, proved uncomfortable when combined with the high G-forces experienced in an F1 car. On some vests the connector has been moved to find a more comfortable position, but the thick material and tubing have also proved cumbersome under the driver’s fireproof overalls. There are also concerns over the reliability of some systems and the possibility that a failure will mean the vest will have the opposite effect and work as a heat insulator.preferring to spend that money instead on car upgrades. The money to develop the vests comes out of the budget cap.

But Russell added that the FIA should make the tech mandatory and develop it themselves, describing this race as like being in a “sauna”.The Briton’s comments prompted a sarcastic response from Verstappen - who doesn’t wear the vests either, out of choice - who said Russell “shouldn’t make a fuss”.

“I don’t need it,” Verstappen said. “Maybe I suffer a bit less from the heat.. I find a Finnish sauna at 85 degrees a lot hotter... You shouldn’t make a fuss. Yes, it is hot, but that’s part of it. You have to train for that.”

The Dutchman added: “When I was 18, I had a bit more trouble with these conditions. But after that, I started training more in the heat, such as in the sauna and a steam room, so that I can handle the sweating better and the fact that your head gets very hot. Maybe I should take him (Russell) to the sauna a few times.”

These two have history, of course. They’ve sniped at each other for years. In 2024, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, it reached a peak when Verstappen described Russell as being “two-faced” and said he had lost all respect for him. Russell responded by saying Verstappen was “a bully”. Earlier this year, the Mercedes driver said Verstappen could always retire from the sport and drive sports cars if he didn’t like the regs.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

News.title: Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade
News.content:
We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

News.title: Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying
News.content:
The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

News.title: Bath complete revenge mission on Exeter despite imperious Feyi-Waboso
News.content:
Bath held off a furious comeback from Exeter, led by the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, to avenge their Gallagher Prem semi-final defeat here in June.

It felt as if lightning might strike Bath twice. Once again Exeter overturned a 26-10 half-time deficit, to manufacture a second-half lead thanks to a pair of blistering finishes by Feyi-Waboso. Four months ago, Bath failed to take a drop goal in the closing stages, but this time with the reassuring presence of Finn Russell at fly-half, they kept their cool.

The Scotland playmaker twice sent penalties deep into the Exeter 22 from where Stephen Varney conceded a yellow card and penalty try before Bath replacement Ted Hill powered through a thicket of Exeter tacklers.

“Finn is one of the best 10s in the world and I thought he had a very good game,” Johann van Graan, the Bath head of rugby, said. “His decision making is above most players in the world and I thought that came through tonight.”

Despite the appearance of yet another high-scoring shoot-out, both teams defended with real bite, although Bath struggled to lay a finger on Feyi-Waboso who ended up in a scrap with a fan in the stands here when he was a spectator in May. He exacted a measure of revenge beating eight defenders and carried for 132 metres.

“Manny still needs game time,” Rob Baxter, the Exeter director of rugby, said. “When he’s on the ball, you see something incredible, but it is his ability to get on the ball again. He is just getting his game minutes and match fitness up.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco, which is placed between the cheek and lower gum, is particularly popular in south Asia. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

Sports.title: Man City HAVE to go down – everyone knew what they were doing, blasts former Prem manager who lost star player to them
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Leeds chief Jesse Marsch has launched a scathing attack on Manchester City – and sensationally claims other clubs were aware of regulation breaches.

An independent commission sent shockwaves through football when they found the Etihad giants guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules.



And Marsch, 52, reckons top-flight chiefs should throw the book at City despite an appeal being launched following the bombshell verdict.

The American failed to steer Leeds to Premier League safety during the 2022/23 season.



It came after City snatched key man Kalvin Phillips away from Elland Road in a monster £45million deal.

Marsch has blasted the Sky Blues, who were found guilty of more than 100 charges, and reckons they deserve to face relegation.

The Canada boss told The Guardian: “I think City should be punished severely.

“I think they should have to go down, and by the way, everyone knew about it. Everyone knew.

“That summer [2022], us and City were the only teams that said we made money.

“For us, we did make money, because we sold Raphinha, we sold Kalvin Phillips.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“We had a lot left over from what we bought. At the time, we weren’t in a position financially to not save.

“Our ownership didn’t have deep pockets. Whereas when City says this, I was literally like, ‘Are you kidding me? Is this some kind of joke?’

“When they said they got Erling Haaland for £51million, it’s like: ‘Yeah, OK, sure!’

“I knew there were inconsistencies in it, but what can you do? You just put your arms in the air and go, ‘This is football’.”



The Premier League revealed City hid an eye-watering £900M in “sham” deals during a nine-year period.

But Sky Blues bosses insist they are innocent and will fight to clear their name.

Sports.title: How Jude Bellingham is going from ‘scapegoat’ to GOAT as Thomas Tuchel finds formula to manage England talisman
Sports.content:
Next

FROM “scapegoat” to GOAT. From “repulsive” to resplendent.

Jude Bellingham is properly on his way to fulfilling his staggering potential which only a year ago looked under threat, not least because he was not getting on particularly well with manager Thomas Tuchel.



On a night of many incredible performances in the 7-0 humiliation of Croatia, super-human Bellingham was the absolute star and over-ran Luka Modric, a former winner of the Ballon d’Or.

England team-mate Harry Kane is up for that award in London later this month but Bellingham, 23, will definitely hold that trophy – along with a few others – if he continues to keep improving like this.



It is remarkable when you consider that when England flew to Miami for the World Cup warm-up on June 1, it was 50-50 whether he would even start the first match against Croatia with childhood pal Morgan Rogers a rival.

Yet manager Tuchel has been rewarded for giving Bellingham some tough love even though it was a gamble and could have gone one of two ways.



In June 2025, Tuchel revealed on talkSPORT that his mother found some of the player’s on-field behaviour repulsive.

Even going back to Euro 2024, when Bellingham was playing for Gareth Southgate, it was clear he was not enjoying playing for England and later claimed he was made a “scapegoat” for the team’s failure to win the tournament in Germany. Bellingham, though, was talking nonsense.

Tuchel apologised to Bellingham for his comments but for a man who speaks better English than some of his players, the former Chelsea boss knew what he was saying.

Exactly 12 months ago, Bellingham was left out of the squad for the Wales and Latvia games as he continued his return to fitness from a shoulder operation. Bellingham later claimed he asked to be left out but it was obvious there was a problem between these two men with strong personalities.

Yet Bellingham, like any great player, upped his level at the right time and let his boots do the talking. In this case, it was the World Cup where he scored seven goals and was England’s best player. It may have helped that he went into the tournament fresh as he had been sidelined for Real Madrid with a hamstring injury.

There were still moments of friction between Bellingham and Tuchel but we must get used to that.

However, Tuchel has now discovered how to manage Bellingham better. As the manager said: “It’s better if he plays with a bit of rage. It’s what he does. I think sometimes he is looking for these moments to get his fire going.”

Nevertheless, Tuchel will sometimes push a button which triggers Bellingham.

Following the 2-1 win over Norway in the quarter-finals, Tuchel called the display sloppy.



Bellingham snapped: “Maybe he doesn’t know what it takes to play in those conditions against Erling Haaland, Nusa, Sorloth – that’s not an easy team to play against.”

Yet providing everything is forgotten, there is no harm done. Bellingham has impressed for new Real manager Jose Mourinho who wants the player to remain as a no 10 and not defend as much as he has previously at the Bernabeu.

With England, at times, he is now playing as a fellow central striker with Kane which is why the pair delivered so much damage in Rijeka and will hope to do the same against the Czech Republic tomorrow.



Pundit Roy Keane, after watching Bellingham score once and deliver three assists, said: “Outstanding in every aspect, I think Bellingham can go on to be one of the greatest players of all time.”

So could Bellingham, currently on 59 caps, end up being the GOAT? He must definitely keep that fire in his belly but also put the team before himself, something which was an initial concern for Tuchel.

An impressed England team-mate Alex Scott said: “Honestly, I’ve never seen anything like it.

“He’s even better in person, seeing it up close and being on the same pitch as him.

“He’s the best midfielder in the world, one of the best players in the world for sure and a great human being.



“Everyone knows that – the fans know that, everyone in the world knows what he’s like as a person.

“On the pitch his ability is scary and that’s the benchmark we need to live up to.

“I’m the same age as him but for me he’s a role model for young English players.”

But the German came under fire when Harry Kane and Co fell to an agonising semi-final defeat against Argentina.



Taylor still thinks Tuchel’s cut-throat personality is exactly what England need as they push for silverware.

And the Thailand assistant boss, who had one showdown in caretaker charge of the Three Lions in 2000, is backing the former Chelsea supremo to seal Euro 2028 glory.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson reveals bizarre Skyscraper photo threat to Man Utd stars who dodged tackles
Sports.content:
Next

SIR ALEX FERGUSON says he used a famous photo to make sure his Manchester United stars would not shirk a challenge.

The legendary Old Trafford chief, 84, guided the Red Devils to a stunning 13 Premier League titles.



And Ferguson, who has revealed dementia fears, refused to let standards drop before quitting in 2013.

The iconic Scottish supremo would invite United’s up-and-coming talents into his office for face-to-face talks as they attempted to make the grade.



He would point to a famous 1932 photo, known as Lunch atop a Skyscraper, to make sure members of his squad were not a bag of nerves.

Ferguson told The Observer: “I liked to get players in my office. I liked to talk to them.

“I did that sometimes with the younger ones. I would tell them a story or something.

“On my wall, I had a photograph of when they were building the Rockefeller Center, when the workers are sitting way up on the girder.

“See that [in the photo]? Not a bit of fear. And I’m asking you to go out there [on the pitch]. If I ever see you jumping out of a tackle, I’ll take you [up] to that [girder].

“The other thing I stuck to was being consistent. I never changed in my beliefs, with young players, whether I was at St Mirren or Aberdeen or United.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“It was always there. I thought it was right. I thought it was good to produce young players.

“I produced dozens of players from the United academy who became internationals, which is pretty good.”

Ferguson has revealed David Beckham, who was among the young gems he brought through the ranks, feared he was being forced out when he was shipped on loan to Preston.

Fergie added: “He thought I was trying to get rid of him, which was not true.



“David was the last to really develop because of his physique. Although he grew to 6ft, he was small and thin as a young kid.”

Ferguson sensationally considered leaving football and moving to Canada before going on to become a hugely-decorated boss at United.

Sports.title: Solly March opens up over Brighton exit heartache as free transfer agent reveals secret summer medical at Prem rival
Sports.content:
Next

SOLLY MARCH has learnt just how ruthless football can be over these past few months.

After 13 years at Brighton being “protected” from the game’s cut-throat nature, the winger was let go by the only professional club he has ever played for in the summer.



It has been a disorienting period which has left him having to go the extra mile to prove to prospective new clubs he is fit enough and still good enough to cut it at the top level.

That in itself has been challenging, given his struggles with a knee injury over the last three seasons.



Even when undertaking a rigorous medical at a Premier League club this summer – which was successful – no contract was forthcoming.

At 32, and with 194 games in the Premier League goals already under his belt, some might be inclined to quit following his injury setbacks.



But March insisted: “Giving up hasn’t been on my mind. I’m quite a determined, stubborn person.

“I just want to prove to myself and to other people that I can get back to where I know I can.

“I’ve never been in this situation, I’ve always been at Brighton, I’ve never had less than two years left on my contract.

“I’ve been tucked away and protected from it all, in a sense. Ninety per cent of footballers probably go through this every year.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“You just see how ruthless it is and people who are involved in it, they’re all in it for themselves, I guess.”

Born in Eastbourne, March was picked up by Brighton in 2011 having been spotted playing for nearby part-timers Lewes as a teenager.

He looked close to an England call-up in 2023 when he was flying under Roberto De Zerbi, before his injury problems began.

He made just 24 appearances in the last three seasons, but even so, March was under the impression that a new deal with Albion was in the offing at the back end of last season following talks with boss Fabian Hurzeler.



Opening up exclusively to SunSport, March said: “From the conversations I had, it sounded positive that there would be some sort of solution for me to be here for what would have been next season and this season.

“I can recall a family BBQ, and even my wife having this conversation with the manager that, yeah, it looks positive, I think next season hopefully still here, I’ve had the conversation, I think everything looks good.

“Even going into the last week of the season, I had a conversation with the technical director where I said, ‘Look, I need a decision, I need to know where I am next season, I need to know where I’m playing my football, I want to know. I don’t want to know last minute’.

“They said, ‘We’re not going to exercise your contract extension because your money will go up and you haven’t played enough games, we don’t think, to earn that’. I was fine with that.

“But he said we don’t not want you here next year so things might have to look a little bit different. We’ll have to have a meeting and talk about how a contract could look.



“I was fine with that because I just wanted to be at the club, I wanted to prove myself again and prove that I’m fit and that I can still produce at the top level.”

March then played in the final game of the season against Manchester United, where he was presented with a shirt to mark his 300th appearance for the club, before heading off on holiday.

The winger continued: “On Monday morning the day after the final game of the season, at 9 o’clock, they rang my agent and said, ‘No that’s it, you’re done. Your time is finished at the club. We’re sorry, that’s it, but that’s how it’s going to be’.

“It wasn’t the decision itself that hurt, because that’s fine, that’s football.

“I didn’t agree with it, I still think I could have made an impact this season.



“But it was the way it was done which probably hurt the most. It still hurts now, to be honest.”

March is at a loss to explain why there was an apparent change of heart from Brighton, but wishes they had told him earlier so he could play some reserve games to aid his cause in finding a new club.

He added: “I want to say I had many great years at Brighton and many great memories.

“The fans have always been amazing with me and still are. The club hierarchy are great people and I wish them all the success this season.

“I don’t think they meant to lead me on for two months. I don’t think they were straight up lying to me or leading me on. I don’t think that was the case.



“But it’s strange they maybe weren’t honest a bit earlier.

“It would have given me a chance to maybe play games for the Under-21s to get some minutes to show other clubs that I am fit.

“I don’t think it’s helped my situation very much, the way it was dealt with, because I’ve not been able to play many minutes.”

March’s knee injury first flared up in 2023, requiring surgery, but on reflection the winger feels he may have come back too early.

Another op, which took place in Germany, was later required but now March feels he is fully over his crock problems.



He has been keeping himself fit in Dubai and in Doha, and confessed to becoming a “geek” by investing in a GPS vest to record his data, to prove his fitness to interested clubs.

March passed a thorough medical at one Premier League club earlier this summer but the team ended up not offering a deal as they failed to offload other players and there was not enough room for him in the squad.

It means the South-Coast lad is still on the lookout for a new home – and would be open to opportunities abroad.



March is currently training with a Championship club to maintain his fitness, with his physical testing and training output understood to be hitting top Premier League physical metrics.

His recently-recorded top speed of 35.4kmh is very close to matching his all-time high.

He added: “Clubs trusting my body and trusting that I can produce week in and week out with training and playing, that’s been the one challenge with most of the people I spoke to.

“They’ve all said the same thing, that it’s not a question of quality, it’s just a question of your body and how much you can take.

“I think I’m in a good position, I really am. My knee is happy and strong, there’s no swelling. I can do all the things that I need to do and very well.



“I had a medical at a Premier League club and it was all good but for various reasons nothing happened from it.

“But the medical was all good. To see that was a positive for me, that my body is passing these things.

“I still believe I can play in the Premier League, I really do. I had a conversation with a player at Brighton a few weeks and was asking him about a manager from a club abroad that was interested because he’s from that country.

“He said to me on the phone, ‘Solly, you could still play for us, you really could. I’m surprised you’re still not here.’

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s a good thing but it’s also a bit frustrating at the same time.



“I’m open to stuff abroad, for sure. I just need to play for a few months and show people I am fit and can still play. Hopefully that option will come soon.”

Sports.title: Premier League icon, 39, SACKED from first-ever manager job at non-league side after just one win in 12 games
Sports.content:
Next

LEE CATTERMOLE has been sacked as the boss of non-league side Gateshead.

The Sunderland legend was only named manager of the National League outfit in June.



But barely three months later, he has been dropped by the team – which sits rock-bottom of the division.

The club have managed to secure just one win in their 12 league games so far this season, while losing on ten occasions.



Saturday’s 2-1 defeat to Worthing appeared to be the breaking point for the club hierarchy, who dropped the axe the day after the result.

Cattermole’s assistant Martin Smith will also be leaving the club with him.



Interim club chairman Graham Wood wrote: “The club wishes to thank Lee and Martin for their efforts, and wishes them both success in their future careers.”

Fellow former Black Cats star Ben Clark has stepped in to helm the side on an interim basis until a new manager can be found.

The troubling news was immediately followed up by a concerning update regarding the club’s ownership situation.

Director Mark Nellist resigned and declared his intentions to withdraw his financial support for the club earlier this week.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The move came after the club was unable to pay its staff’s wages in September.

And now it has been confirmed that Nellist is hoping to gift his shares to fellow shareholder Stephen Paylor, pending approval by the Independent Football Regulator.

But the club also revealed that they understand Paylor will not be able to provide the missing funding without the aid of a would-be third party whose interest in investing in the club has cooled – casting doubt on whether the IFR would sanction the share transfer.

Sports.title: Sale defy Vermeulen's first-half red card to beat Saracens
Sports.content:
Sale Sharks won a real battle against Saracens in the Gallagher Prem

Sale defied Jacques Vermeulen's first-half red card to dispatch Saracens 21-17 with Tom O'Flaherty emerging as the star of a slugfest at StoneX Stadium.

Vermeulen was shown a 20-minute red for a dangerous tackle on Tomos Williams at a point in the first half when Alex Lozowski was in the sin bin because of the same offence.

Saracens then took control but it was only temporary and in the 41st minute O'Flaherty produced the match's pivotal moment by racing over for a dynamic solo try.

It was part of a dominant second half from Sale, who capitalised on the hosts' lifeless performance to bounce back after losing to Bristol on the opening weekend with their hooker Nathan Jibulu also outstanding.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Referee Joe James and TMO Hamish Smales experienced a busy opening half an hour, issuing two cards and disallowing a Saracens try.

It had started so well for Sale when Jibulu finished a driving maul but soon after centre Lozowski was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on Alfie Barbeary, who was forced off for an HIA.

Worse was to come when Vermeulen was given his marching orders for a dangerous challenge on Williams as the Sharks looked to press home an attack down the right touchline.

It meant Saracens were given the opportunity to play against 13 for three minutes and Sale's situation would have deteriorated further had Courtney Lawes not seen an attempted deliberate knock go backwards.

Almost immediately the hosts appeared to have taken advantage but a Nick Tompkins try was ruled out because of obstruction by Nick Isiekwe and it was not until Eroni Mawi bundled over in the 34th minute that they were off the mark.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

For all Saracens' sustained pressure they still trailed 7-5 and a minute into the second half that became 14-5 after O'Flaherty caught a George Ford up and under that went sideways and then slipped through the home defence before sprinting over.

Sale ran out of tacklers to enable Sione Va'enuku to strike back almost immediately but they resumed on the front foot and were frustrated to be penalised just short of the whitewash on two occasions.

They continued knocking on the door and suddenly changed pace with a series of runs gaining yards until Ford sent Ben Bamber galloping over.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Sale now led 21-10 and Saracens' dismal afternoon continued when Theo Dan limped off while his fellow hooker Jamie George watched from the stands, sidelined by injury.

Charlie Bracken combined with brother Jack to race over with eight minutes to go and the Sharks then let another commanding position slip away because of a penalty close to the line, but they had already done enough to see off Saracens.

Sports.title: Taylor stars as Colts cruise past Commanders in NFL's return to London
Sports.content:
Jonathan Taylor scored twice as Indianapolis Colts overcame Washington Commanders 30-13 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to open this year's triple-header of NFL International Series games in London.

The Commanders initially had the better of things, limiting the Colts offense to 20 total yards in the first quarter as they claimed a 6-0 lead.

But an injury to QB Marcus Mariota when sacked on the play prior to Washington's second field goal proved a turning point, with third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis - a seventh-round draft pick - unable to lead the Commanders to victory despite a couple of eye-catching plays, including a 47-yard deep-ball TD for his first in the NFL.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Washington Commanders rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis finds Treylon Burks for his first NFL touchdown

Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, who had two turnovers in the first half, ran in Indianapolis' third touchdown of the game early in the fourth quarter to stretch their lead to two scores - and there was to be no way back for Washington.

Image: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones dives in for the game-clinching touchdown in the fourth quarter

The NFL returns to Tottenham next Sunday for a clash between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars, who are back in action facing the Houston Texans at Wembley a week later, on Sunday October 18.

The Colts fell behind early when Jones lost the football after he was accidentally tripped by his own team-mate, with the Commanders scoring a field goal after Odafe Oweh recovered the ball at the 20-yard line.

Mariota, filling in for injured starting QB Jayden Daniels, left the game with a knee injury when sacked on the play prior to Washington's second field goal.

Kaliakmanis came in, the 223rd overall pick from the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and though he found the going tough early on his NFL debut, Colts veteran Jones was similarly struggling and was picked off by Rasul Douglas.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonathan Taylor runs into the end zone for the Indianapolis Colts' first touchdown in their NFL clash with Washington Commanders in London

But the Colts soon took over again on downs after the Commanders' call to go for it on fourth down from their own 46-yard line. It would prove a poor decision, helping set up Taylor's opening TD for Indianapolis to see them into a lead that they stretched to four by the half with the first of Spencer Shrader's three field goals. Taylor celebrated his score by pantomiming drinking tea in the end zone.

Kaliakmanis threw a costly interception early in the third quarter, with Taylor's second five-yard scoring run of the game then making it 17-6.

Kaliakmanis bounced back on the next drive, though, hitting Treylon Burks on a stunning, 47-yard touchdown pass deep down the left sideline that closed the gap as Burks got past star cornerback Sauce Gardner.

But the Colts (2-2) answered back with further Shrader field goals either side of Jones' touchdown run from four yards out early in the fourth quarter.

Sports.title: Labuschagne hits timely ton as Australia warm up for South Africa Tests
Sports.content:
Marnus Labuschagne scored a speedy, and timely, century in Australia's sole warm-up match before the three-Test series in South Africa from Friday, live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Labuschagne struck 111 from 89 balls, reaching three figures from 76 deliveries and hitting 19 fours, before retiring out against a Cricket South Africa Invitation XI in Potchefstroom.

The 32-year-old will hope to carry that form into the Test arena, starting in Durban this week, having gone 43 innings and over three years without a hundred in the format.

After Labuschagne - who is averaging 25.43 since the 2023 Ashes - made scores of one, 31 and four in the recent 1-1 series draw at home to Bangladesh, ex-Australia captain Ricky Ponting told Sky Sports that the batter's spot in the XI had become "untenable".

However, the Baggy Greens have kept faith with the South Africa-born player and he seems set to line up in his usual No 3 berth at Kingsmead as Australia begin their first Test series in the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.

Image: Steve Smith will play Test cricket in South Africa for the first time since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal

Smith scores half-century in Test tune-up

Steve Smith - who along with David Warner and Cameron Bancroft received a ban for the role he played in using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball - Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and Matt Renshaw are the survivors from that contest eight years ago.

Smith, who followed Labuschagne in retiring out, and Renshaw scored 61 and 32 respectively on the second and final day of the tune-up for this month's Tests, while Alex Carey made 57 as Australia replied to the hosts' 318-7 with 368-6.

On day one, Australia used 11 bowlers in order to manage workload with seven taking a wicket apiece and none of the seamers getting through more than 10 overs.

Image: Josh Hazlewood was one of a plethora of bowlers used by Australia on day one of the tune-up fixture

All-rounder Cameron Green did not feature after picking up an abdominal injury in the final ODI against South Africa last week and appears a doubt for the first Test.

After the series opener in Durban, the teams will meet in Gqeberha from October 18 and then Cape Town from October 27.

South Africa also host Bangladesh and England in Test cricket this winter, with the series against Joe Root's men starting at Wanderers in Johannesburg on December 17.

Watch the first Test between South Africa and Australia live on Sky Sports Cricket from Friday (7.30am on air, 8.30am first ball).

Djokovic is a record six-time champion in Beijing and had won all 29 of his previous matches at the tournament before returning this year for the first time since 2015, when he defeated Nadal in the final to claim his sixth title.

"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn't feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.

"I gave him an early break and then it was hard to come back in the first set. I had a couple of break points when he was serving for the set at 5-4, but didn't use them, but I kind of felt already from midway through the first set that I was starting to get a good rhythm, at least one my serve and on serve plus one."

Meeting for the first time in ​nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German's power in the early stages as Zverev claimed the ​opening set, but the Serb gradually ⁠worked his way into the ⁠match and refused to let his opponent pull away.

The turning point came late ‌in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his ‌favour after a tightly contested battle.

With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break ⁠to seal victory.

The pair had not met ​since last year's French Open, where ​Djokovic won in four sets, and this encounter ​again highlighted the Serb's ability to deliver under ⁠pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the win, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh ⁠China Open title and an elusive ​first trophy of the year, while denying Zverev ​another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world No 1 ranking.

Djokovic's next assignment will be a meeting with Daniil Medvedev, who earlier overcame Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.

He is just the third man in ATP history (since 1973) to earn a top-three win after turning 39 years of age, after Ken Rosewall and Jimmy Connors.

"To be honest, these are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said.

"The motivation is big obviously when you are feeling good and competing at par with the best players in the world, in front of 15,000 people of course. These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player. It's been a struggle this year, to be honest, for different reasons, but I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money. I'm just glad to push it through."

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, former British No 1 Annabel Croft described the match as an "incredible contest".

"Some high-quality, absolutely fantastic tennis between two brilliant players. Why would you ever doubt Novak Djokovic even at the age of 39?

"The match got better and better as well, and had some different tactical shifts for Djokovic, who after the long physical points, I thought his legs were tiring, but he came back. He threw in some drop shots, he threw in some serve and volleys early in the second set and just changed things up with the pattern of play.

"Djokovic came up with the answers. It was on a knife edge right to the end but what a finish and what a treat for all those fans in Beijing."

Sports.title: Daryz retains Arc crown with dazzling display
Sports.content:
Daryz became the first colt for almost 50 years to win Europe’s most prestigious race, the Qatar Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe, in successive seasons with a brilliant victory at ParisLongchamp.

Not since the Vincent O'Brien-trained Alleged and Lester Piggott in 1977 and 1978 has a colt managed to defend his title, but once Mickael Barzalona pulled the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained Daryz out to make his run the result looked inevitable.

The Prix Foy proved the key form guide, as Daryz beat George Scott's Bay City Roller in that trial and those two filled the same positions again in the main event, with Aidan O'Brien's Diamond Necklace running a fine race in third from stall 16.

Barzalona said: "To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse.

"It was a really tough race, it didn't go as we expected but he showed his talent and that made the difference in the end.

"The pace was not strong, it was a rough race and nothing went to plan, but the horse deserved to win again and he's proved all season he is the best one. I'm delighted."

Graffard said: "He's a good horse, he's a champion. I said that before, it's rare I'm confident before a race as it is so hard in a race like this, but I knew things were going right and he'd be very hard to beat.

"I was confident. but I was putting so much pressure on myself before the race and you can make yourself look a fool so it is easier not to speak and not say anything.

"But I think for the sport we have to be transparent and I was confident and his rider was confident so we had to say it.

"Mickael rode a beautiful race again. It's so beautiful for the sport, I'm lucky to have horses like that."

He added: "It is different when you are favourite and you are the one to beat. There was pressure, you can't deny it, but it's good and it's why I show emotion. It's great for the owners (Aga Khan Studs), it's such a wonderful breeding operation.

"We kept losing position early, we were too far back but we were lucky Daryz has good acceleration. Without any trouble I knew he'd run a big race. I'm lucky to train a horse like this and I hope I get plenty more!

"I don't think he has to prove anything else."

Sports.title: Meronk outlasts Jarvis to win Alfred Dunhill Links Championship
Sports.content:
Adrian Meronk came from four shots behind to overtake Casey Jarvis and win the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship by two shots on a gripping final day at St Andrews.

The victory saw the LIV Golfer end a 1,078-day wait to claim his fifth DP World Tour title and regain his tour card for next season, as the Polish golfer posted a final-round score of 68.

Jarvis held a two-stroke lead coming into day four at St Andrews, and after getting off to a fast start with back-to-back birdies on holes four and five, he slumped, making bogeys on holes nine and 11.

A thrilling finish unravelled, with Meronk, who held a two-shot lead going into the final three holes, giving Jarvis a chance to cut the gap on the 17th after the Cleeks GC player carded a bogey.

But Jarvis couldn't move within one shot, with the South African missing the green on the penultimate hole, going down for a bogey.

It meant he would go down the fairway on the 18th needing to make an eagle to force a play-off, and despite driving to the fringes of the green, he was unable to sink a long, winding putt on the last, ultimately confirming Meronk's victory.

Jarvis, who posted a final round 72, would finish tied for second with Niklas Nørgaard, who carded three birdies in his final five holes to surge up the leaderboard.

World No 979 Michael Stewart enjoyed a fairytale week at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, as the 36-year-old, who was playing on the Tartan Pro Tour last week, placed tied for fourth with Tommy Fleetwood, at 16-under.

Brooks Koepka earned his first top-10 finish on both the DP World Tour and PGA Tour since March, with the American joining last year's Alfred Dunhill Links Champion Robert MacIntyre at 16 under to tie for sixth place.
