Sports.title: “I guess it’s my fault” says Norris as stewards reprimand him for near-miss under Safety Car | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris admitted he was caught out by how quickly the field slowed ahead of him during the Safety Car period.

The McLaren driver almost ran into his team mate Oscar Piastri as they approached turn one in the queue behind the Safety Car. The incident occured as George Russell ahead of them slowed unexpectedly and came to a stop on the right-hand side of the track next to the pit lane entrance.

Norris said he noticed the Mercedes slowing but was unsure how much the cars ahead of him were reacting.

“I couldn’t see from the angle, and just from where I was, how much everyone had stopped because of George on the inside,” said Norris. “By the time I kind of looked at George and looked back, I could see them, but it’s hard when you’re directly behind to see if they’re going 100 [kph], 200 or 10.

“They were going 10, so I just got completely caught out. I guess it’s my fault in the end of the day. I was just unlucky with it everyone just checked up so much and I just got screwed over by it, that’s all.”

Norris narrowly missed hitting Piastri, ran onto the gravel trap on the outside then rejoined the queue having lost several places.

The stewards have summoned Norris for “driving erratically under Safety Car conditions, leaving the track and re-joining unsafely and/or overtaking another car behind the Safety Car.”

Alexander Albon is also under investigation for driving erratically in another incident which involved Piastri. The Williams driver, who was following his team mate Carlos Sainz Jnr into the pits during an earlier Safety Car deployment, appeared to slow, causing Piastri to take avoiding action.

Update: Norris has been reprimanded for his incident and Albon has been cleared.

Stewards’ verdict on Norris

While following the Safety Car, [Norris] approached turn one behind a group of cars. Car 63 (George Russell) had stopped with a mechanical problem ahead of turn one, which caused the cars ahead of Norris to slow down. Norris explained that, due to the low sun and resulting visibility conditions, it was difficult to recognise that the cars ahead had started to slow earlier than would normally have been expected. Norris consequently misjudged his closing speed and approached the cars ahead too quickly. When he realised this, he braked heavily and deliberately steered to the left, onto the kerbs and then into the gravel bed in order to avoid contact with the cars ahead. By driving onto the kerbs, Norris had reduced grip available for braking, which further limited his ability to slow the car. In doing so, Norris momentarily overshot car 81 (Oscar Piastri), who was directly ahead of him. The stewards considered whether this constituted an overtake while the Safety Car was deployed. Although Norris momentarily moved ahead of Piastri, this occurred solely as a consequence of Norris leaving the track while taking avoiding action. [Piastri] immediately repassed Norris while Norris was off the track. The stewards therefore determined that this did not constitute an overtaking manoeuvre and take no further action in respect of this aspect of the incident. The stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car, Norris should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with greater care. The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which Norris should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap to the cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving. The need for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that Norris had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had driven erratically in breach of Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Such a situation should not arise while driving behind the Safety Car, and Norris was required to maintain a sufficient margin to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that Norris reacted promptly once he recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the stewards consider a reprimand as appropriate. The stewards separately considered Norris’s return to the track. Although car 18 (Lance Stroll) was in relative close proximity, Norris returned progressively and without requiring [Stroll] to take avoiding action or otherwise creating an unsafe situation. The stewards therefore determined that the re-join was safe. The stewards also reviewed whether, after having re-joined the track, Norris had overtaken Stroll while the Safety Car was deployed. The video evidence showed that, as Norris returned from the gravel, he had already crossed the white line with at least one wheel and, as such, was back on track. At this point, he was ahead of Stroll and at no point did Norris pass Stroll. Rather, Stroll approached Norris while Norris was already in the process of returning to the track. The stewards therefore determined that Norris had not overtaken Stroll under Safety Car conditions and as such also take no further action for this part of the incident. Accordingly, the stewards impose a reprimand on Norris for erratic driving. No further action is taken in relation to the re-join or the alleged overtake while the Safety Car was deployed.

Stewards’ verdict on Albon

On the approach to the pit entry, [Albon] reduced his speed, causing Piastri, who was following closely behind, to brake and take avoiding action. No collision or contact occurred. Albon explained that immediately before entering the pit entry road he became aware that he was below the required delta time and therefore reduced his speed in order to comply with the applicable delta requirement. Piastri confirmed, having heard Albon’s explanation, that he considered the reason for Albon’s actions understandable. While the situation required a significant reaction from Piastri and could potentially have developed into a dangerous situation, the stewards were satisfied that Albon’s actions were taken in an attempt to comply with the applicable delta requirements and explained the otherwise unusual reduction in speed at that location. His actions, therefore, did not constitute erratic or unnecessarily dangerous driving in the circumstances. Having considered the matter extensively, the stewards determine that no infringement occurred and accordingly take no further action.

Sports.title: Hadjar had “no battery” to defend from Hamilton and Leclerc in final laps | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar said he was unable to defend his podium position in the final laps of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The Red Bull driver held third place behind his team mate and Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the final Safety Car period. However he had both Ferraris close behind him.

Once the race restarted, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc quick picked him off. Hadjar took the chequered flag in fifth place.

Hadjar successfully resisted Hamilton for many laps earlier in the race when his rival was on the medium tyre compound. However once Hamilton switched to soft tyres under the Safety Car, Hadjar fell prey to the Ferrari.

“I had no battery, something like that,” he explained. “So there was no contest against the Ferraris in the straight.”

However Hadjar was unhappy with his pace earlier in the race as well. “I don’t know what happened in terms of the grip I had on the car,” he said. “The whole race I was so slow.

“I don’t know what happened to my pace, but [it] really [was] one race to put in the bin.”

“We’ll fix the issue and understand why we are so bad today,” he added.

Sports.title: Wolff calls Mercedes’ Sepang race “one of my worst experiences” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff was deeply unhappy with their performance in today’s race.

The two W17s hit the front of the field immediately after the start. However Andrea Kimi Antonelli fell to second place behind Max Verstappen at the finish and George Russell retired shortly before the finish.

Antonelli increased his championship lead over Russell and Lewis Hamilton, though the latter recovered from a significant delay at the start of the race to salvage third place.

“I’m so massively annoyed and not in a happy place,” Wolff told Sky.

Mercedes introduced a significant upgrade for their car this weekend but appeared to gain little from it. “First of all, we didn’t have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend,” said Wolff. “So there’s a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I’m sure we will.

“Then the race literally went – if you consider the fight with Lewis behind – went against us. We had such an advantage. Two VSCs or one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn’t be more unlucky.”

Russell’s retirement – his third in a grand prix this season – leaves him 84 points behind Antonelli in the championship fight.

“To make things worse, a PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points,” Wolff continued. “So as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences to be honest.”

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker’s Next Fight Has Three Options
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn floated Conor Wallace, Anthony Yarde, and the winner of Joshua Buatsi against Willy Hutchinson as the potential next steps for Ben Whittaker. Taking the Wallace rematch makes the most sense because it directly answers the questions raised by that shaky finish in Birmingham last night.

Whittaker left with the decision, yet Wallace buzzed him in round ten, turning the final minutes into a desperate scramble to survive. Jumping immediately into a premier domestic clash invites serious danger before Whittaker proves he can fix those defensive holes.

“For me, no, he needs another fight. Now when I look at it, I think that’s the [Joshua] Buatsi-[Willy] Hutchinson winner, that’s [Anthony] Yarde, or it’s Conor Wallace,” Hearn said post-fight about Whittaker’s next opponent.

Wallace carries built-in drama for a second meeting. He knows he can rattle Whittaker, while Whittaker knows he can dominate the rounds when boxing on his terms. A return bout tests whether Wallace brings heat from the opening bell, and whether Whittaker maintains focus once under fire.

A basic points win changes little. Whittaker must command the championship rounds, clear his head instantly when tagged, and shut down sustained rallies after eating a clean shot.

Facing Joshua Buatsi or Willy Hutchinson is an immediate leap into danger. Both carry the thump and ring wisdom to punish defensive lapses, and neither will give away the opening half of a contest the way Wallace did. Even the loser of that matchup represents an unnecessary hazard.

Anthony Yarde offers an empty proposition. His name still resonates with British audiences, but stoppage losses to Artur Beterbiev and David Benavidez offer critics an easy asterisk. His heavy hands remain real enough to flatten Whittaker, leaving high physical risk without the sporting credibility to match.

That leaves Wallace as the most useful next opponent. Keeping the rematch in Birmingham could build on the first fight’s drama while giving Whittaker a familiar setting to show improvement.

A controlled twelve-round performance would provide stronger evidence for the next step up. Hearn has bigger names available, but Wallace has already supplied the test Whittaker needs to pass more convincingly.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Expects Los Angeles Meeting With Dana White
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn expects to meet Dana White in Los Angeles next week to discuss his involvement in Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua. Before agreeing to a role, Hearn wants to know what Joshua and Matchroom would receive in return.

That question gives the proposed meeting a purpose beyond settling their public argument. Hearn is leaving room for an agreement while using his claimed contractual veto to negotiate terms.

“What’s in it for Anthony? What’s in it for us?” Hearn said during his post-fight media session in Birmingham. “And once we establish that, we can make a decision. … They cannot be involved in the fight unless myself and Anthony allow them to be.”

Asked whether White would attend the Los Angeles meeting, Hearn said he was “supposed to be.” The meeting remains proposed rather than confirmed.

Hearn says Turki Alalshikh and Netflix want White involved. If his account of the contract is accurate, that gives Matchroom something to bargain with. Their preference for White doesn’t automatically supply a reason for Joshua’s side to accept him. Hearn could seek financial terms, promotional support or another concession, although he hasn’t disclosed any demands. His willingness to meet allows him to hear a proposal while keeping pressure on White to explain what he contributes.

The television production dispute adds another complication. Hearn claimed Sela had told him in writing that White’s statement about handling production was untrue. He maintained that the contract prohibits that involvement, although the relevant terms weren’t presented during the interview.

An appearance at a press conference and responsibility for producing the broadcast would involve different responsibilities. Any agreement would need to establish the scope of White’s role. Hearn also recognizes the promotional value of their rivalry. He acknowledged that the dispute has helped the buildup and said he wants to question White directly if they share a press conference stage.

That gives both sides a reason to find an arrangement. White could gain a visible role in the event, while their exchanges could attract further attention. Hearn’s position is that Joshua and Matchroom should receive a benefit for allowing it. The Los Angeles meeting could establish whether White’s side has an offer he considers worthwhile.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Revives Shakur Stevenson Fight Speculation
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s Instagram promo featuring Shakur Stevenson puts a potentially lucrative matchup back into circulation as his inactivity approaches a year. Their stalled fight offers Haney a recognizable opponent, a winnable contest, and a way to regain attention after months on the sidelines.

Haney shared footage showing him facing off with Shakur, reviving speculation about their fight without confirming that negotiations have resumed. Devin’s side previously appeared willing to accept 144 pounds, but the fight never materialized. If talks restart, the camps would need to clarify whether Haney is still willing to fight at that weight.

The weight remains a potential obstacle. Haney would likely prefer 147 pounds, where he could face the smaller Shakur without cutting extra weight. Shakur previously wanted 144. Agreeing to that would mean Haney coming down three pounds, although we do not know whether the extra weight cut would weaken him.

😈😈😈😈😈 @Realdevinhaney LETS GO!!!! — Shakur Stevenson (@ShakurStevenson) October 4, 2026

Haney’s jab and reach give him a chance to beat Shakur without having to chase him. He can stay outside and make Shakur come forward to land punches. Both prefer opponents to attack first, so the fight could become cautious, with neither throwing much. Whoever lands his jab more consistently could win those close rounds.

Haney also needs to capitalize on his victory over Brian Norman Jr. from last November. Nearly eleven months have passed since he picked up the WBO welterweight belt. Crossing the November 22 mark without an opponent locked in burns an entire year of his prime. That kind of layoff wastes prime earning power, halts development inside the ropes, and chips away at fan interest.

Viable alternatives exist near 147 pounds if Shakur remains occupied with Gary Antuanne Russell. Richardson Hitchins, Liam Paro, Lewis Crocker, Teofimo Lopez, Jack Catterall, and Arnold Barboza Jr. all represent credible pairings, provided schedules cooperate. Haney has plenty of directions to turn, but he cannot afford to let another month slip by without putting a date on the calendar.

Shakur can pursue another title at 140 against Russell or revisit a potentially bigger payday against Haney. The Haney fight would require him to move up in weight against a larger opponent, making the catchweight agreement a major part of any renewed negotiations.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Calls Anthony Joshua A Usyk Warm-Up
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury is already looking past Anthony Joshua toward a trilogy bout with Oleksandr Usyk. He treats their December 11 Cardiff clash like tune-up work for a champion who already beat him twice.

That gives Joshua a golden opportunity to wreck everything. A loss completely ruins any market for another Usyk meeting, especially after Fury spent weeks dismissing Joshua as light work.

“I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk,” Fury told Sky Sports.

Fury wants the Usyk trilogy in New York. He also points to his activity this year, including fights with Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, as evidence that he will enter the Joshua bout ready.

Staying active helps Fury shake off ring rust, but Joshua brings threats none of those recent opponents offered. Joshua carries genuine power. Fury cannot afford to look past him or script future dates while dodging heavy artillery. A single defensive lapse ends all talk of a third Usyk clash instantly.

Joshua hits hard enough to test whether Fury still has elite reflexes over 12 rounds. Usyk is an entirely different animal. He relies on rapid footwork, awkward southpaw angles, non-stop punching. Fury could beat Joshua easily, but that does not solve the tactical problems that cost him against Usyk twice.

Winning in Cardiff gives Fury a huge name to brag about. It proves nothing about how a third fight with Usyk would turn out.

Fury’s trash talk is pure fight promotion. He degrades Joshua to sell the Cardiff gate while teasing an even bigger event down the line. His bravado sells tickets, but talk alone proves nothing about the reality inside his training camp.

If Fury wins, he could try to sell a big victory, but Usyk still holds two decisions over him. The champion would need serious motivation to face a boxer he conquered twice.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez Managers Meet
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez’s manager Keith Connolly has met with Ryan Garcia’s manager Lupe Valencia and teased a “mega fight.” However, making Garcia–Lopez could require Teofimo to give up his WBA welterweight title, with Jack Catterall’s mandatory defense due.

The money fight can happen without two belts. The question is whether Teofimo can take his WBA championship into it while Catterall insists on getting his opportunity.

“Met up with Lupe Valencia today in San Diego for coffee,” Connolly wrote on Instagram, in a screenshot shared by Dan Rafael. “Boxing fans get ready Mega Fight coming.”

Connolly did not identify the matchup or announce an agreement, but meeting with Ryan’s manager and posting that caption gives Garcia–Lopez speculation something more substantial than another exchange of callouts.

It does nothing to settle the Catterall situation.

Teofimo and Catterall have until October 22 to negotiate a deal for their WBA title fight before the organization can move toward a purse bid. Catterall has made clear he won’t step aside, leaving Teofimo’s team with an obligation that a separate agreement with Ryan would not erase.

Unless the WBA grants permission for Garcia–Lopez to go ahead first, Teofimo could have to sacrifice his belt to pursue it. The deadline itself would not automatically strip him, but signing for Ryan would still leave the mandatory unresolved.

From a business perspective, losing the WBA title might be a price Teofimo is willing to pay. Ryan offers a commercially attractive opponent, and his WBC championship would give Teofimo another title to chase if the fight proceeds as a sanctioned defense.

That would change the promotion from a welterweight unification to a challenge for Ryan’s belt, without necessarily reducing the fighters’ interest in making it.

Connolly’s post suggests there is something to watch. Until the Catterall obligation is addressed, though, the two-title billing remains uncertain.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Offered To Stage Bentley–Hernandez In Ghana
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley had an offer from Eddie Hearn to defend his WBO middleweight title against Yoenli Hernandez in Ghana before choosing Zuffa Boxing. Hearn revealed that Bentley requested a meeting with Matchroom, opening discussions about a route that would have included fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bentley instead signed a multi-fight Zuffa agreement and will face Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena. That provides a different opponent and promotional future, although his WBO title situation remains unresolved.

“Denzel Bentley asked for a meeting with us,” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “He was going to fight the mandatory in Ghana on our Ghana show. He chose to accept a little bit more money and … vacate the belt. … You blow the belt for nothing, for an extra 50 grand. I mean, it’s just madness.”

Hearn did not disclose Matchroom’s total offer or the terms beyond staging the Hernandez defense in Ghana. His £50,000 comparison therefore gives only part of the financial picture. A multi-fight agreement also requires Bentley to consider future purses, opponents and opportunities.

Hearn believes Bentley would beat Hernandez. I would favor the Cuban, whose pressure, combination punching and power could make the mandatory a demanding defense. Bentley would need to produce enough offense to discourage Hernandez while avoiding prolonged exchanges that suit the challenger.

That difference in how the fight is viewed helps explain the decision. Hearn sees a title Bentley should retain; Bentley may see a dangerous obligation alongside an alternative that offers greater financial security.

There is also a qualification to Hearn’s claim about vacating. Bentley has reportedly petitioned the WBO to approve Mosley as a voluntary defense, with his title at risk if permission is refused.

The Ghana proposal shows Bentley had another option. Whether it was the better one depends on more than the immediate purse difference Hearn described.

Sports.title: Andy Lee Reveals Ben Whittaker’s COVID Before Wallace Fight
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s trainer, Andy Lee, said the unbeaten light heavyweight had COVID the week before facing Conor Wallace. Whittaker offered a different explanation for his difficult finish in Birmingham on Saturday: the fight had been “too easy,” and he lost concentration.

Dan Rafael reported Lee’s disclosure after Whittaker’s points victory, adding that both sides were discussing a rematch. The illness claim provides context for Whittaker’s performance, although how much it affected him remains unclear.

Whittaker sounded eager to face Wallace again rather than leave the late rounds as the final impression of their IBF eliminator.

“I think we should do it again and I’ll beat him down even better,” Whittaker said afterward. “If I’m honest, it was too easy. I took my eye off the ball a little bit and he come up with a good shot. That’s boxing. But what did I do? I dug it out and I won.”

That explanation reflects how comfortably Whittaker controlled much of the contest, but it understates the danger Wallace created late. Whittaker was hurt and had to survive an opponent who kept pressing after spending the earlier rounds struggling to reach him.

Lee’s account and Whittaker’s explanation can both be true. An interrupted preparation could have left him below his best, while lapses in concentration gave Wallace opportunities. However, the reported illness cannot tell us which mistakes came from his physical condition and which came from his decisions.

Calling the fight easy also gives Whittaker something to prove in a return bout. Winning the early rounds comfortably is only part of the job. Maintaining distance, following instructions and avoiding unnecessary exchanges become more valuable when an opponent starts landing.

A rematch would give Wallace another opportunity after his strong finish and allow Whittaker to show whether he can sustain his early control over 12 rounds.

For a fighter pursuing a world title, that would be useful evidence. Whittaker proved he could survive trouble on Saturday. Facing Wallace again would test whether he can prevent it.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Rejects Dana White’s Fury–Joshua Production Claim
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn claims Sela has denied in writing that Dana White will handle television production for Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua. However, Hearn remains open to negotiating White’s involvement and expects to meet him in Los Angeles next week.

That leaves White’s role unresolved. Hearn is challenging his claim to an existing production role while asking what Joshua and Matchroom would receive in exchange for agreeing to his participation.

“After that video, I spoke to Sela and I said, ‘Have you seen this video?’” Hearn told the post-fight press conference in Birmingham. “And they said, ‘Yes, and it is completely untrue.’ And they told me that in writing. … He cannot do that under the contract.”

That is Hearn’s account of Sela’s response and the contractual restrictions. The written communication and relevant contract wording were not presented during his remarks.

Hearn also acknowledged that Turki Alalshikh and Netflix want White involved. Their interest gives the proposed Los Angeles meeting a purpose: finding terms that satisfy Joshua’s side while allowing White a place in the event.

For Hearn, the question is what that participation adds. He asked what would be in it for Joshua and Matchroom, suggesting that permission could depend on a tangible benefit rather than simply accommodating the wishes of the other parties.

He conceded that the public dispute has helped the promotion. That creates an incentive to reach an agreement, particularly if an appearance by White generates more attention. Hearn wants freedom to question him directly if they share a press-conference stage.

The production claim nevertheless concerns a specific responsibility, beyond appearing at promotional events. Hearn’s remarks leave room for White to secure an agreed role later, but challenge the suggestion that television production is already his responsibility.

The proposed meeting could settle that difference. For now, Hearn’s position is that any involvement requires agreement from him and Joshua, with the benefits explained before they give their approval.

It also called on NPP members to support the new executives and work together in a spirit of unity.

Ghana News.title: Dr Antwi-Boasiako’s cybersecurity book showcased at UN crime prevention congress
Ghana News.content:
Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako

A book documenting Ghana’s cybersecurity development, authored by former Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority, Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako, has been exhibited at the 15th United Nations (UN) Congress on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice in Abu Dhabi.

The book "The Republic", a professional journey, Ghana’s cybersecurity and the making of a role model country, was among the selected publications displayed at the congress, held in the United Arab Emirates from September 26 to October 1, 2026.

The event brought together more than 5,000 participants from about 97 countries, the release said.

Published in November 2025, the professional autobiography traces Dr Antwi-Boasiako’s career alongside the development of Ghana’s cybersecurity institutions, policies and initiatives. It also documents the contributions of public officials, industry players and international partners to that process.

The book’s selection followed a recommendation from members of the United Nations Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice (CCPCJ) community.

In a letter cited in the release, the Chair of the commission’s 34th session, José Antonio Zabalgoitia, described the selected publications as accounts that highlight courage, determination and resilience, while reinforcing the pursuit of just and peaceful societies.

The letter also described The Republic as a valuable addition to an exhibition intended to strengthen international cooperation in addressing public security challenges.

Reacting to the selection, Dr Antwi-Boasiako credited the people and institutions whose work contributed to Ghana’s cybersecurity development.

“THE REPUBLIC is a record of work that was never mine alone. It reflects the efforts of many colleagues, partners, and public service officials who helped build Ghana’s cybersecurity foundations,” he said.

“To see the book being selected by the United Nations Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice was entirely unexpected, and I accept the honour on behalf of everyone who shared in that journey.”

The exhibition offered delegates an opportunity to explore Ghana’s cybersecurity experience through the author’s first-hand account.

Following the congress, the exhibited copy is being retained in an Abu Dhabi library as part of the CCPCJ’s historical collection, according to the release.

The book explores the challenges, decisions and partnerships that shaped Ghana’s cybersecurity development, presenting lessons for policymakers, professionals and public sector leaders.

Ghana News.title: We will empower the grassroots and protect every vote – NPP’s 1st Vice Chair Kojo Bamba
Ghana News.content:
Newly elected National First Vice Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Kwadwo Fosu Boadu, popularly known as Kojo Bamba, has pledged to prioritise the grassroots and protect the party’s votes as the NPP begins preparations for the 2028 general election.

In a message posted on Facebook after his election on Sunday, October 4, after his elections, Mr Boadu said strengthening the party at the grassroots would be a key priority as the party prepares for 2028.

He said the grassroots would need to be empowered to play an effective role in the party’s activities, while measures would also be taken to protect the party’s votes throughout the electoral process.

“The journey to 2028 starts now. We will empower the grassroots. We will protect every vote. We will work as one family,” he said.

“Together, we can win!” he added.

Mr Boadu expressed gratitude to delegates for electing him and said he was deeply humbled by the confidence they had placed in him.

“I am deeply humbled and grateful to the delegates of the New Patriotic Party for the confidence reposed in me as the newly elected National 1st Vice Chairman,” he said.

Read also: From Delta Force to NPP First Vice Chairman – Kojo Bamba’s political journey

Mr Boadu said his victory should not be seen as a personal achievement, but as a victory for the party’s grassroots members, constituency executives, youth and women’s organisers, and delegates who supported his vision.

“This victory is not mine alone. It belongs to every grassroots foot soldier, every constituency executive, every youth and women’s organiser, and every delegate who believed in the vision of protecting our ballot boxes from the polling station to the collation centres,” he said.

He pledged to take up the responsibility with humility and a commitment to serving the party, while working with the new national leadership to strengthen the NPP.

“I accept this responsibility with humility and a firm commitment to serve,” he said.

Mr Boadu said he would work with the newly elected National Chairman, John Boadu, and the rest of the national executive to rebuild and unite the party ahead of the next general election.

“Together with our new National Chairman, John Boadu, and the entire national executive, we will work tirelessly to rebuild, unite, and strengthen our great party,” he said.

Mr Boadu, who rose from the party’s grassroots to become one of its national executives, secured 3,116 votes to emerge first among 13 candidates contesting the three Vice Chairmanship positions at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi on Saturday, October 3.

From Delta Force to NPP leadership

Mr Boadu’s political journey began at the grassroots and included a controversial period as leader of Delta Force, a pro-NPP vigilante group that gained notoriety in the Ashanti Region after the party’s 2016 electoral victory.

A former auto mechanic, he led the group during a period of heightened political tension, including opposition to the appointment of George Adjei as Ashanti Regional Security Coordinator.

Read Also: From Delta Force to NPP First Vice Chairman – Kojo Bamba’s political journey

In 2018, Mr Boadu was appointed Deputy National Director of Operations of the NPP’s youth wing, marking his transition into the party’s formal structures.

During his campaign for the First Vice Chairmanship, he placed particular emphasis on grassroots mobilisation and the welfare of constituency executives, describing them as the party’s frontline workers.

His election now places him among the NPP’s national leadership as the party prepares for the 2028 general election.

He will serve alongside newly elected National Chairman John Boadu, Second Vice Chairman Henry Nana Boakye and Third Vice Chairman Nana Akomea.

Mr Boadu ended his message by stressing the broader purpose of his new role:

“The NPP must rise again in 2028, not just for political power, but for the countless dreams and destinies that depend on a brighter future.”

Ghana News.title: Police blur the line between invitations and arrests – Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah
Ghana News.content:
Legal practitioner and Acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC), Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah, has criticised law enforcement agencies for blurring the distinction between inviting citizens to assist investigations and placing them under arrest.

Speaking to Samson Lardy on The Law on JoyNews on Sunday, October 4, 2026, he said the practice had created apprehension among people who might otherwise be willing to assist investigations.

Mr Twumasi Ankrah explained that an invitation could be a request for information or documents to help investigators establish the facts, without the person being treated as a suspect.

However, he said some people honoured such requests only to discover that they were no longer free to leave.

“More often than not, you are invited, and being a law-abiding citizen who wants to see that justice is done or that truth is ascertained, you attend the invitation only to go there, and after giving the information that the police require from you, you are told you can’t leave,” he said.

He argued that once a person’s freedom to leave was restricted, law enforcement officers must recognise the change in circumstances and take steps to safeguard the person’s constitutional rights.

“At that particular point in time, the police is required by law to take certain steps to ensure that your constitutional rights are safeguarded. But mostly the police blur the line,” he stated.

Mr Twumasi Ankrah acknowledged that inviting someone to assist an investigation was generally a prudent approach, particularly when investigators had yet to determine the person’s role in a case.

He said the difficulty arose when invitations routinely resulted in arrests, leaving citizens uncertain about what to expect.

“They have so often turned an invitation into an arrest that the people have now become apprehensive,” he said.

According to him, the uncertainty had prompted some people to decline invitations and wait for law enforcement agencies to exercise their powers of arrest.

He said citizens were consequently trying to balance their willingness to assist investigators with the need to protect their liberty.

“There is this genuine fear… that when they go, there is a likelihood they won’t come back home. So, the police also have some work to do in that regard,” he added.

The legal practitioner advised people attending police invitations to seek legal assistance, explaining that their status could change during questioning.

“You go with your lawyer to pre-empt anything that may happen which was not within your contemplation,” he said.

He stressed that legal representation could help individuals understand their position in an investigation and assert their rights if an invitation developed into an arrest.

Ghana News.title: Turning invitations into arrests is making citizens reluctant to assist police – Twumasi Ankrah
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Reindorf Twumasi Ankrah has warned that the practice of arresting people after inviting them to assist investigations is making citizens increasingly reluctant to cooperate with the police.

Mr Twumasi Ankrah, who is the acting Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC), said the uncertainty surrounding such invitations had created fear among people willing to provide information to investigators.

Speaking to Samson Lardy on The Law on JoyNews on Sunday, October 4, 2026, he argued that law enforcement agencies must address the apprehension their practices had generated.

“The practice has shown over the years that when people willingly submit themselves or attend to an invitation extended to them by the police or any other institution with the power to effect arrest, they end up being arrested,” he said.

According to him, some citizens now prefer to wait for a formal arrest rather than voluntarily honour an invitation that could result in unexpected detention.

“So, with the benefit of that practice, people now have also taken a position not to honour such invitations and to say to them that you come and now exercise your powers of arrest; then they know that properly they are a suspect,” he explained.

Mr Twumasi Ankrah acknowledged that invitations were a legitimate and prudent means of obtaining information, particularly when investigators had not established whether an individual should be considered a suspect.

An invitation, he explained, could simply require someone to supply documents or clarify facts relevant to a case involving another person.

However, he said the repeated use of invitations that subsequently led to arrests had undermined citizens’ confidence in the process.

“They have so often created, turned an invitation into an arrest that the people have now become apprehensive,” he stated.

He said this had left citizens balancing their willingness to help investigators establish the truth against concerns about their personal liberty.

“There is this genuine fear as to whether it is imminent or remote, that when they go, there is a likelihood they won’t come back home. So, the police also have some work to do in that regard,” he said.

Mr Twumasi Ankrah advised individuals to seek legal representation when attending an invitation, given the possibility that their role in an investigation could change.

“You go with your lawyer to pre-empt anything that may happen which was not within your contemplation,” he said.

He further argued that once officers prevented an individual from leaving, they had to recognise the change from voluntary attendance to detention and safeguard the person’s constitutional rights.

Ghana News.title: The Traffitech-GH SMS spot-fine system: The good, the sad, and the funny – Bright Simons writes
Ghana News.content:
The carnage on Ghana’s roads is not a joke. Road crashes killed 2,949 people in 2025, up from 2,494 the year before.

Serious injuries rose to 16,714. Many people believe that bad motorist behaviour has a big part to play, and that the Police are either too stretched thin or too corrupt to effectively enforce deterrence.

So when the government announces that it is deploying technology to improve the situation, it is hard to argue with the logic. However, there were some murmurings about poor sensitisation.

The Police took the cue and postponed implementation by a month. We now have to wait until 1st November 2026 before the police start fining motorists by text message.

Cameras and handheld devices will catch vehicles speeding, jumping red lights, and committing more than 45 other offences, and the registered owner will get an SMS with the fine and 14 days to pay.

How are we going to use the one month to influence how the program shapes up? On my part, I see a teaching moment for katanomics (www dot katanomics dot org).

The katanomic framing of the SMS-spot-finding initiative is that, as usual, the political vision is easy to sell (stop road carnage). It is a simple WHAT message that rallies the people.

The HOW – the realm of POLICY – is where things usually start falling apart. Because POLICY takes a simple goal and unravels it into many complex parts, some of which are in tension. THE DEVIL IS ALWAYS IN THE DETAIL. Since you’ve read up to this point, you asked for it.

1. The journey to the Traffitech-GH system surprisingly started around 2008, nearly 20 years ago. Implementation of the idea of using cameras to catch traffic violators and issue spot fines has had a bumpy ride.

2. The person who has kept it going is a gritty entrepreneur who has survived the NPP – NDC rollercoaster that has quenched so many business dreams. His name is Frank Osei. The heart of his empire is Nationwide Technologies.

3. He sold the tax stamps and fuel marking to the NDC in the Mills era. The NDC were slow to get either to a serious scale. The NPP came and bulldozed them through. He pushed the public-private partnership (PPP) concession for the text-messaging spot-fine system during the NPP era and helped get the agreement signed in 2022. The NPP was sluggish in deploying it. The NDC seems determined to bulldoze it through.

4. As I said, Mr Osei set up Nationwide Traffic Management & Enforcement Limited (NTMEL) in 2008 and started pushing aggressively. As was the case with the tax stamps and fuel marking projects he helped broker with the government, he ended up needing a foreign technology partner from Sweden, a company called Sensys Gatso.

5. The origin of Sensys Gatso is actually in 1950s Holland, where a relentless speed-racing driver, Maurice Gatsonides, decided to invent an automated speed-tracking technology to sustain his impossibly high standards.

6. Sensys Gatso’s TRaaS and related technologies will, initially, be deployed in Ghana primarily in the form of fixed cameras at about 34 hazardous junctions, ~20 in-vehicle cameras, ~30 handheld laser cameras, and tripod units to record offences.

7. Officers also log offences on handheld devices. Images will go to regional back offices, where police review them before a notice is sent by SMS from “GPS-MTTD”. Owners can pay through http://Ghana.gov, mobile money or *222#, or contest online and attend a hearing at an MTTD station. MTTD is Ghana’s transport police.

8. Camera fines start at GH¢120 for the first three offences, then GH¢180 and GH¢240. A sixth offence within 24 months can go to court and cost a licence for at least a year. After 14 days, 1 per cent of the fine is added every day, so an unpaid GH¢120 fine becomes GH¢240 after 100 days of default. No cap has been published.

Unpaid fines can block DVLA services, and officials have floated restrictions linked to the Ghana Card. The registered owner is liable “regardless of who was driving”.

10. The first time Ghana really got serious about doing this was in 2016 when an agreement was reached to deploy in 2017. In April 2018, the President’s road-safety action plan directed a partnership with “private towing companies and NTMEL.” GH¢335 million a year was promised for three years, partly to pay for road signs and markings, and the techie stuff. The towing scheme collapsed that year. The rest crumbled on cue, though some people got “warning text messages.”

11. By the end of 2021, the Ministry of Finance listed the project as an unsolicited proposal under negotiation at an estimated US$9.9 million.

12. As mentioned earlier, the current PPP agreement was signed on 23 December 2022 for eleven years (to December 2033) with a reported investment cost of GH¢77.73 million (about $7.3 million then). Caution notices began in June 2024, and by the end of 2025, about 120,000 had been sent.

13. The law itself came last. The Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, passed in December 2025, mentions automated enforcement once, by adding that a “spot fine” includes an automated fine. Owner liability, the daily surcharge, licence penalties and camera evidence are all perching in regulations passed in 2026 (L.I. 2519).

14. Note the classic katanomics: the contract, whose economics depend on fines, was signed three years before the state had the regulations to levy them.

15. I find it puzzling that Police and ministers seem so guarded about explaining this history. They regularly refer to “a private sector partner” and provide no further details.

16. Yet Sensys Gatso has been very open about the whole commercial apparatus.

17. NTMEL’s shares are split exactly 60 per cent to Mr Frank Osei and 40 per cent to Sensys Gatso International B.V., part of the Swedish-listed Sensys Gatso Group, as aforementioned.

18. The Ghanaian majority is, however, only part of the picture. The Board is split right down the middle. Lewis H. Miller, who became chief executive of Sensys Gatso Group in June 2025, and Timo Gatsonides, one of Sensys Gatso’s largest shareholders, hold the fort for the Swedes on NTMEL’s 4-person Director list.

NTMEL’s managing director, Edmar van der Weijden, is also managing director of Sensys Gatso International, the 40 per cent shareholder. A former Sensys Gatso chief executive is registered as a beneficial owner of NTMEL with the right to appoint and remove directors.

20. Sensys Gatso also supplies the cameras and software, and has said it expects to earn from hardware sales and licence fees on top of its share of profits.

21. Like the Margins-run “Ghana Card”, the whole Traffitech-GH scheme is fundamentally commercial. The revenue comes from fining people and is split 40 per cent to the private party and 60 per cent to government. That is to say, if you are dumb enough to text whilst driving, you will be putting a cool ~50 GHS into the pocket of Mr Osei and his Swedish partners for each text.

22. Sensys Gatso has told its investors to expect about SEK 600 million (~$60 million) in joint-venture revenue over the rest of the contract. Its 2025 annual report shows NTMEL had no revenue in 2024 or 2025, lost SEK 5.9 million (~$600k) in 2025, and ended the year with SEK 2.9 million in cash. The operator needs fines to flow.

23. The government’s 2022 PPP report lists “revenues from traffic fines for Government” among the benefits it expects to maximise. Finance Ministry mandarins are sitting there with a calculator waiting for clowns to jump red lights.

24. I will admit it, I am a bit uneasy about this. Not because I have sympathy for red-light jumpers. I just think that when the operator’s income rises with every fine-ticket, the pressure is to put cameras where tickets are plentiful rather than where people die, to tighten thresholds of offending, and to resist appeals.

25. Uganda’s version of this model reportedly gave its foreign operator 80 per cent of fines and was suspended within days of launch in June 2025 because of such perverse incentives.

26. I also think that the investors have been waiting to rake in revenue before bothering to invest. The whole operation feels too barebones given the scale of the problem. It is true that Ghana already has thousands of outdoor cameras. But these are Chinese-vendor-supplied national security cameras that are unsuitable for Traffitech-GH for many reasons, including privacy and the lack of special traffic-monitoring-focused features. This means NTMEL must deploy a ton of cameras and personnel to review the footage/images. So far, they appear to be waiting for the fine revenue to go through the roof before doing this.

I also worry about enforcement quality. Sending a text message to people in a country like Ghana to pay a fine is literally daring them to ignore, wait, and see. Would we then rely on the same Police we are replacing with tech due to their supposed ineptitude, incapacity, and/or corruption to go around forcing people to pay?

28. The idea of hooking this up to drivers’ licenses and Ghana Card sounds brilliant in theory, but it runs heavily into the serious informality that attends every aspect of our lives in Ghana. Unlike elsewhere, people don’t have to encounter the formal system regularly to survive. The same reason why, despite repeated “mass registrations”, we keep hearing that the Ghana Card system is porous is the reason why relying on civil identity platforms would, in my humble view, prove less robust than we think.

29. The 2024 pilots showed that missing owner information in DVLA records, and insurance records still bearing brokers’ phone numbers instead of owners’, are rather pervasive issues. Vehicles registered by hand before 2023 are still being re-verified. So, anyone who sold a car without completing the transfer, or changed their number, may learn of a fine only once penalties have piled up.

30. Seven people were arrested in February 2026 for sending FAKE fine notices with payment links. The scammers are already ahead of the system.

31. Another issue is that disputes go to MTTD stations. There is no independent body, unlike South Africa, where a separate agency adjudicates. So, we are back to making this a Police gig.

32. I worry that the basics may not even be in place. Speed enforcement is fair only where limits are posted. Red-light enforcement is smooth only where signals work. Where the infrastructure itself seems designed to promote disorderly behaviour, we may yet find that the system regularly gets overwhelmed by the sheer volumes of recorded violations.

33. It seems very clear to me that the government, and the Police in particular, have a fine one-month opportunity to show that they can rise above katanomics. There are several things they can do to do so.

34. They can publish the PPP contract for further scrutiny; change the terms from a share of fines to a fixed fee to discourage overzealous and commercially minded deployment; tighten the law to avoid abuse of the system to track and spy on people (ensuring that images aren’t passed around to jealous husbands or something, for instance); implement an independent appeals process; publish a risk-based deployment map (i.e. investment in cameras etc., should follow what the data says about the highest risk of road crashes); and outline a safeguarding measure against scams and fraud.

35. Will the Police beat katanomics? Who is up for a bet?

-

Authored by: Bright Simons

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Police investigating Flydubai co-pilot’s Australia ties
World.content:
Australian police and intelligence join the list of those probing the incident.

Authorities have said they are investigating the links of the co-pilot of the Israel-bound Flydubai flight with Australia.

A multi-agency Australian police and intelligence team – the Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – is carrying out the probe, a spokesperson said on Sunday.

Mystery surrounds the co-pilot, who is accused of attacking the captain with an axe and attempting to seize control of Flight FZ1073 from Dubai as it approached Israel, and how he was able to acquire his seat in the plane’s cockpit.

He has been identified in media reports as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami.

He had been barred from flying in his own country because of concerns that he had adopted “extremist” views, The Associated Press news agency cited sources as saying.

While al-Hammami reportedly spent part of his life in the United Arab Emirates, the Reuters news agency, citing sources briefed on the Australian investigation, reported that he studied at a university in the Australian city of Melbourne.

A third unnamed source told the agency that he studied at RMIT University, a public research university in Melbourne, about a decade ago.

The Financial Times also reported al-Hammami’s links to Australia. Citing two sources familiar with the Australian investigation, the FT said al-Hammami had allegedly visited what it described as “radical mosques and extremist websites” while in the country.

Disaster was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot and a reserve pilot took over its controls and completed an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.



However, the case has raised questions about security in Israel, which has some of the world’s strictest aviation security measures.

The prosecutor general of the UAE, Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, has labelled the attack an attempted “terrorist act”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel has longstanding arrangements with foreign airlines aimed at preventing pilots who are nationals of countries without diplomatic relations with Israel from flying there.

Netanyahu said a “loophole” appears to have allowed the Omani pilot to take part in the Flydubai flight, and that Israel would now strengthen its checks.

The UAE has not yet publicly established a motive or announced whether investigators believe al-Hammami acted alone.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Saturday that the latest “terrorist” attack is a new warning that the region’s fight against “extremism” is not over.

World.title: Ukraine ready for US-backed talks with Russia: Zelenskyy
World.content:
Trilateral talks could happen this month in UAE or another US-proposed venue, says the president.

Ukraine is ready to hold trilateral talks with the United States and Russia this month, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said.

The Ukrainian president made the comments on Sunday during a news conference alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Kyiv. He said Ukraine supports a swift timeline for returning to talks to try to end the war fought for over four and a half years.

US efforts to broker a ceasefire have been paused since Washington launched its war on Iran. However, Washington is now pushing for technical-level talks by the end of October, Zelenskyy said.

He confirmed earlier reports that the United Arab Emirates, which has hosted previous talks, could again be the setting for a meeting.

“I confirmed to [the US] that our side is ready to support this timeline,” Zelenskyy said, adding that Kyiv is open to meeting in the UAE or “another country proposed by the American side”.

Washington had also been in touch with Moscow about the plan, Zelenskyy said. The Kremlin said last month that it did not rule out the possibility of three-way talks this month.

Despite suggestions of their willingness to discuss an end to the conflict, both Russia and Ukraine have also said they will ramp up long-range attacks on military and related targets.

Moscow has said it is targeting Ukraine’s energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to minus 20C.

Zelenskyy on Sunday said he was “amazed” by Russia’s “savage desire to escalate the situation every day”.



He yet again accused Moscow of targeting “civilian infrastructure, including data centres and mobile network facilities”.

“Honestly speaking, I am not surprised by this approach to the war – by Russia’s hatred towards Ukraine – but I am surprised by the specific tactics used”, the Ukrainian leader said.

Alongside the return of the US to efforts to broker a ceasefire, India on Sunday said that it aims to step up its efforts to play a larger role in mediating an end to the conflict.

Speaking at the Munich Security Conference in New Delhi, Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said his country had become more involved in recent months, specifically regarding shipping in the Black Sea, which has been plagued by mines and attacks on commercial vessels.

India was also “going beyond that,” said Jaishankar, including with discussions on grain and energy exports and “on non-attack possibilities,” he said.

World.title: Mass protests demanding poll chief resignation shake India for third day
World.content:
Protesters say the election commission’s voter-roll revision has removed millions of eligible voters to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP party.

Thousands of youth and opposition protesters have rallied for a third day in India demanding the resignation of the country’s election commission chief.

Thousands marched in Mumbai on Sunday, while others gathered for a third day of demonstrations in New Delhi. The protests began on Friday demanding that Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down due to reports that he has overseen voter-roll revisions removing millions from electoral lists.

Protesters say the disenfranchisement stands to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the ECI and the BJP have denied the allegations.

Led by opposition leaders Raj Thackeray and Uddhav Thackeray, thousands marched in Mumbai on Sunday, waving Indian flags and calling for Kumar to step down.

In the capital, New Delhi, protesters started gathering in the early evening. As on previous days, some were detained by police as they arrived, according to the Reuters news agency.

Police in the capital have clamped down in a bid to prevent protesters from assembling over the last two days, detaining dozens and taking them away by bus.

Some of the detainees were released later on Friday and Saturday, but police registered cases against some on charges of violating orders banning mass gatherings in the centre of the capital.

“⁠I just want to tell the ruling party this much … We are angry about how you are wielding that power. ⁠It’s the people of this country who should decide who sits in power and who sits in opposition, not the election commission,” Raj Thackeray told the crowd in Mumbai.



The ECI says the voter-roll revision is designed to remove duplicate, deceased or ineligible entries and maintain electoral integrity. On Friday, it directed its officials to register eligible voters inadvertently omitted from electoral rolls.

Kumar has not publicly responded to the demands for his resignation or commented on the protests, which look set to continue over the coming days, with more rallies planned.

An alliance of India’s opposition parties plans to launch protests to “save democracy” with a march to the election commission office on Tuesday. The Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced plans for a major rally in New Delhi on October 10.

“Mumbai is out on the streets again for free and fair elections!” Abhijeet Dipke, chief of the CJP, said in a social media post on Sunday.

“Solidarity with all the protesters,” he added. “All Indians need to come together. It’s now or never!”

World.title: Germany’s Merz in Kyiv announces $1.5B in aid, urges Putin to end war
World.content:
Germany’s Merz in Kyiv announces $1.5B in aid, urges Putin to end war

NewsFeed Germany’s Merz in Kyiv announces $1.5B in aid, urges Putin to end war

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, on a surprise visit to Kyiv, announced $1.5 billion in military and reconstruction aid and expanded drone cooperation with Ukraine, giving Kyiv greater capability to strike deeper inside Russia. He also urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war.

World.title: Air strike in Sudan kills UN aid truck driver: WFP
World.content:
WFP food aid truck attacked in Sudan’s South Kordofan, killing one driver as violence escalates in the region.

An air strike on United Nations trucks has killed a driver in Sudan’s South Kordofan, according to the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP).

The WFP said in a statement released on Sunday that the trucks, carrying food aid, were “clearly marked as humanitarian vehicles” as they came under attack. The agency did not identify those responsible.

The strike hit the convoy on Saturday as it was travelling between two cities controlled by the government’s Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) in South Kordofan state.

Fighting in the Kordofan region intensified in late 2025, turning the territory into a strategic battleground between the SAF and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The two have been fighting for control of Sudan in a civil war that has now lasted more than three years.

The extent of the damage and additional details regarding the attack on WFP aid trucks are still being assessed. The UN agency said that it has called for an investigation.

“These incidents underscore the increasingly challenging security environment in Sudan and the risks that aid workers face when delivering life-saving assistance to communities in need,” the statement reads.

Since the war began in April 2023, one in five attacks in Sudan has occurred in the Kordofan region. The army has the upper hand in the north, having made a series of recent gains, while the RSF maintains control over much of the west. South Kordofan remains contested.
