Both the SAF and RSF have increasingly deployed drones in their war, with attacks on towns in North Kordofan growing more frequent and deadly, and civilian infrastructure coming under attack across the region.



The civil war has forcibly displaced 14 million people, plunging the country into one of the worst modern food crises and killing tens of thousands of people.

Nearly 19.5 million people – about 41 percent of Sudan’s population – were struggling with acute food crises between February and May, according to an Integrated Food Security Phase Classification assessment, a leading authority on global hunger. More than five million faced extreme, life-threatening food shortages, and 135,000 were at risk of famine.

World.title: Man City’s Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest US international goalscorer
World.content:
Cacan Sullivan’s goal came after teenager Julian Hall, 18, had given Mauricio Pochettino’s side the lead in Mexico friendly.

Cavan Sullivan became the youngest US international goalscorer in history as the United States defeated archrivals Mexico 3-0 in a friendly international in Arizona on Saturday.

Sullivan, who is poised to join English Premier League side Manchester City next year, netted a superbly taken goal in the 62nd minute to double the USA lead at the State Farm Stadium in Glendale.

At 17 years and five days, Sullivan beat Mathis Albert’s five-day-old record as the youngest US goalscorer.

Albert, aged 17 and 31 days, scored during Tuesday’s 4-2 defeat of Chile.

“These are the moments you dream of when you’re three, four, five or six-years-old,” Sullivan said.

“I manifested this moment, not just these past couple of hours when I found out I was starting, but my whole life,” he added.

Sullivan’s strike came after another teenager — 18-year-old Julian Hall — had given Mauricio Pochettino’s side the lead in the 28th minute.

Hall’s goal was his third in as many games since being handed his international debut by US coach Pochettino in last week’s defeat of Peru. Hall also scored in the victory over Chile.

The loss puts more pressure on Mexico coach Rafael Marquez, who is still seeking his first win since taking over following the World Cup.

Mexico dominated possession and territory early on but were unable to find a way through a well-organised United States defence.

Instead, it was the hosts who took the lead just before the half-hour mark with a superbly worked goal from Hall.

Gio Reyna surged into the penalty area to collect a pass from Alex Freeman and ghosted past Mexico midfielder Erik Lira to reach the byline.



Reyna’s low cross was parried away by Mexico goalkeeper Raul Rangel, but only as far as Hall, who lashed in from close range to make it 1-0.

Mexico’s best chance came early in the second half when Roberto Alvarado’s rasping shot from the edge of the area was tipped over the bar by US goalkeeper Diego Kochen.

Pochettino’s side doubled their lead on 62 minutes when Sullivan’s persistence in chasing down a long ball was rewarded after Rangel mishit a pass to the American outside his area.

Sullivan coolly took his time and chipped home from long range to make it 2-0.

“I just remember chipping the ball, hoping it didn’t hit the crossbar or go over,” Sullivan said of his strike. “I was getting nervous when it was in the air and then everything was a blur.”

A miserable night for Mexico got worse shortly afterwards when substitute Luis Chavez was shown a red card for shoving a hand into the face of Sebastian Berhalter in the 68th minute.

The United States completed the scoring in the 84th minute when Malik Tillman latched onto a poor Mexico backpass and smashed a shot into the top corner for 3-0.

World.title: Three years of genocide in Gaza through one man’s camera
World.content:
Three years of genocide in Gaza through one man’s camera

NewsFeed Three years of genocide in Gaza through one man’s camera

For almost three years, Ibrahim Rabaa has filmed fragments of his life through Israel’s genocide in Gaza, capturing bombardment and repeated displacement. His footage is a personal record of a war that has killed over 73,000 Palestinians.

World.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
World.content:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit.

Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city.

Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day.

The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times.

"To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday.

Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected.

Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person.

Meanwhile, in the central city of Dnipro, six people were injured after a communications facility was struck, he said.

Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down.

World.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
World.content:
Major bridges in Ukraine have been the target of Russian strikes over the past four days, as Moscow ramps up attacks in Ukraine's capital city.

The Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, has been hit for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier this week.

The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a visit to Kyiv on Sunday.

BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near one of the bridges that was targeted and explains what we know so far.

World.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
World.content:
The head of Yemen's internationally recognised government has announced it will wage an all out war in an effort to take all territory held by the Houthis.

It follows an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in recent days.

The Iran-backed group said it had struck sites belonging to Saudi national oil company Aramco, in response to what it described as 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in 12 hours. Saudi Arabia has yet to comment.

The Yemeni government's fierce statement was expected after the Houthis' offensive last month, which saw them seize control of the country's coastline, including the vital shipping lane of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

World.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
World.content:
Rebel forces in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region have said they have temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital, Mekelle, as fighting with the national army moves towards the city.

The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), which has been running the region, said its decision to relocate was made because of concerns about risks to civilians.

Two residents in Mekelle told the BBC that pro-government forces now control the city and TPLF forces have abandoned it. One resident also said mobile phone services appear to have resumed in parts of the city.

Fighting has erupted in recent weeks between the TPLF and federal government forces alongside allied fighters in parts of Ethiopia's northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

The development marks a major shift in the conflict and raises concerns among observers that the fighting could further destabilise the Horn of Africa, potentially drawing in neighbouring countries.

The US Department of State called for "restraint" and "dialogue" on all sides ahead of a diplomatic meeting about the conflict in Egypt on Sunday with leaders from some of Ethiopia's neighbours.

World.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
World.content:
US murderer Christa Pike remains critically ill in hospital and her prognosis is still unclear following her failed execution, her lawyer has said on Sunday.

Speaking to CNN on Sunday morning, Pike's lawyer Stephen Ferrell said doctors were still trying to clear two doses of pentobarbital from her body.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

She survived two execution attempts on Wednesday, and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee.

Ferrell said: "She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill, we really don't know the prognosis yet, and may not know for several days."

He didn't believe she had regained consciousness at any point, adding that he has been receiving updates through her medical power of attorney rather than consulting directly with doctors.

He has not been in to see her. "She is guarded. I'm not sure who may have seen her," he said.

Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. But Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said he would resign on Saturday.

"If she recovers - she may not fully recover - and there may be issues about her competence. I mean, we just don't know any of this," Ferrell said. "We have had no discussions about this. The Tennessee attorney general's office so far has not given us any indications of what their intentions will be."

World.title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
World.content:
A US Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan, local officials say.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the crime as a "brutal and heinous" robbery and murder. She said she had urged the US to "enforce stricter discipline" of its personnel.

Japan's public broadcaster NHK identified the victim as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma.

"We are actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine," the Marine Corps said on social media, extending condolences to the victim's family.

Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said the woman's body was discovered early Saturday morning in a hotel in Naha City, the capital of the Okinawa prefecture.

"Such an incident is utterly inexcusable and fills me with strong indignation," Koizumi wrote on social media, adding that "incidents and accidents involving U.S. military personnel cause significant anxiety to the local community and must never occur".

The US Embassy in Tokyo said that it was fully cooperating with the Japanese government and local police. Japan's foreign ministry said it summoned US ambassador George Glass to discuss the incident on Sunday.

Okinawa is home to several US military bases and tens of thousands of American troops.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja says the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

"The fact that this kind of event has happened again leaves us no choice but to conclude that the US military's efforts in maintaining discipline, educating personnel, and other such measures are completely ineffective," he said.

World.title: Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest
World.content:
Three female journalists have accused police officers in India of sexual harassment during street protests in the capital Delhi.

The claims were made on Saturday after the force detained scores of young people calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner.

In a post on social media, Delhi Police said its New Delhi District had received the complaint, and it had been transferred to its crime branch for a "fair and impartial" inquiry.

Thousands of protesters gathered in Delhi and Mumbai cities for a third day on Sunday demanding that Gyanesh Kumar step down over large-scale changes to voter rolls.

The Election Commission says the exercise is intended to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.

Videos online show people being physically dragged away from the Jantar Mantar protest site in central Delhi.

The accusations by the women journalists include inappropriate touching by some police.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said women fear for their safety and the home ministry must "answer for this".

"Police dragged me by my hair," Aahna Singh, an activist and student at Jawaharlal Nehru University told Reuters news agency during the protests.

She said the police were resorting to "brutality".

The Press Club of India has demanded immediate action on the complaints against police officers, saying it was "shocked and dismayed" by the treatment of journalists.

"Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy. Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues," it said in a statement.

World.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
World.content:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.

In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".

The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".

Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.

Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Oscars 2027: Nigeria submits Dear Ajayi for international feature category
World.content:
The Nigerian Official Selection Committee (NOSC) has chosen Damilola Orimogunje’s Dear Ajayi as Nigeria’s official submission for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards.

The committee announced the decision after reviewing films submitted during its month-long call for entries, which ran from 1 to 31 August.

Its selection places Dear Ajayi in contention for consideration by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences ahead of the 99th Oscars, scheduled for 14 March 2027 in Los Angeles.

The selection does not, however, constitute an Oscar nomination. The Academy will assess the film’s eligibility alongside submissions from other countries before voting determines the 15-film shortlist and, subsequently, the five nominees.

NOSC Chairperson Stephanie Linus congratulated the filmmakers and expressed the committee’s support as the production entered the next stage.

“We look forward to presenting the film for the Academy’s consideration and wish the team every success in the next stage of the process,” she said.

Nigeria returns to Oscars race

The selection marks Nigeria’s return to the Oscars process after the country failed to submit a film for the 98th Academy Awards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In 2025, the NOSC review committee said none of the entries it considered demonstrated the required level of “creative and technical intentionality.”

The committee subsequently opened submissions for the 99th Academy Awards on 1 August, giving Nigerian filmmakers, producers, and rights holders until 31 August to enter eligible productions through its portal.

NOSC is recognised by the Academy as the body responsible for choosing Nigeria’s official entry in the International Feature Film category. The committee has overseen the country’s participation in the category since 2019.

Each year, a country or region can submit only one film through its Academy-approved selection committee. (thenosc.org)

Dear Ajayi

Written and directed by Mr Orimogunje, Dear Ajayi is a Nigeria-Germany co-production set in southwestern Nigeria in the 1990s.

The family drama follows Ade and Titi Ajayi, two estranged sisters forced to live together and care for their paralysed mother.

Ade, a devout Christian and the family’s breadwinner, struggles to understand Titi, an aspiring singer whose independent spirit challenges the expectations placed on her.

Their reunion brings old resentments to the surface, compelling both women to confront the grief, family history and conflicting ambitions that drove them apart.

The film combines Yoruba, English, and Igbo dialogue and explores family responsibility, faith, ambition, sacrifice, forgiveness, and reconciliation.

Its cast includes Bimbo Akintola as Ade, Tosin Adeyemi as Titi, and Lanre Hassan as their mother. William Benson, Antar Laniyan, Uzoamaka Power, Michelle Dede, and Chioma “Chigul” Omeruah also feature in the production.

The film featured in the competition section of the 2026 Giornate degli Autori, an independent programme held alongside the Venice International Film Festival. It is also scheduled to screen at Film Africa in London on 30 October.

Eligibility requirements

Under the Academy’s rules, an international feature must run for more than 40 minutes, be produced outside the United States and contain more than 50 per cent non-English dialogue.

Nigerian Pidgin English qualifies as a non-English language under the rules.

Entries must also carry accurate, legible English subtitles and complete a commercial cinema run of at least seven consecutive days at one venue before being released on television, streaming services, or the internet.

A prior television, online or streaming release can make a film ineligible under the theatrical-release pathway.

New festival pathway

For the 99th Academy Awards, the Academy introduced an additional qualification route for international feature films.

Under the new rule, a film not submitted through its country’s selection committee or that does not meet the normal theatrical-release requirement may still qualify independently by winning a designated award at an approved international film festival.

The qualifying festivals include Berlin, Cannes, Venice, Sundance, Toronto and Busan.

Nigeria’s Oscar history

Nigeria has not received a nomination in the Best International Feature Film category.

Its first entry, Genevieve Nnaji’s Lionheart, was disqualified from the 2020 Oscars because the Academy determined that most of its dialogue was in English.

Desmond Ovbiagele’s The Milkmaid was accepted as Nigeria’s entry for the 93rd Academy Awards but did not progress to the 15-film shortlist. Mai Mataiba also lost out in the 2025 Oscar race.

World.title: Osun govt seeks reversal of court order restricting state’s bank accounts
World.content:
The Osun State Government has asked the Federal High Court in Lagos to vacate an order restricting its bank accounts over a $13.9 million arbitration award in favour of Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, a contractor involved in water infrastructure projects in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

According to a statement signed by the state’s Commissioner of Information and Public Enlightenment, Oluomo Kolapo Alimi, and shared with PREMIUM TIMES, the government filed the application on 2 October, arguing that Gamji allegedly failed to disclose material facts when it sought the account restriction.

The state said one of the undisclosed facts was that it had already approached the Lagos State High Court to challenge the arbitration award before Gamji sought the Federal High Court order.

Mr Alimi said the state’s legal team filed the suit to set aside the arbitral award at the Lagos State High Court on 1 September, while an application was also filed to suspend enforcement of the award pending the determination of the case.

“The Counsel to the State Government had filed the suit to set aside the Arbitral Award at the Lagos State High Court since the 1st day of September, 2026 – prior to the time when Gamji Nig. Co. Ltd. surreptitiously approached the Federal High Court to deceitfully procure an ex-parte order,” Mr Alimi stated.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Federal High Court had ordered commercial banks to place a “Post No Debit” restriction on accounts operated by the state government to preserve $13.9 million and N157.5 million awarded to Gamji.

The interim order, issued by Judge Daniel Osiagor, followed an application by Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, seeking to preserve the funds pending the determination of its motion on notice. The court adjourned the case until 22 October.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Alimi said the applications challenging the award were served on Gamji and its lawyers before the company approached the Federal High Court.

He, however, stated that the company failed to disclose the pending challenge when it sought the interim restriction on the state’s accounts.

“The state government submitted that just as the court order was a product of deceit and substantial non-disclosure of material facts to the Court, the arbitration award it sought to enforce was also fraught with several irregularities,” Mr Alimi said.

Dispute over arbitration award

The dispute arose from two water infrastructure contracts awarded to Gamji Nigeria Company Limited by the Osun State Government in 2017 during the administration of former Governor Adegboyega Oyetola.

The projects involved the construction of transmission mains and booster pump stations, as well as water reservoirs in Ilesa West Local Government Area.

Gamji Nigeria Company Limited, in its suit marked FHC/L/CS/1233/2026, told the Federal High Court that the projects were funded through an Islamic Development Bank loan facility facilitated by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

The company said the original contracts were initially valued at $15.98 million and $9.70 million, respectively, before subsequent variations increased their values.

It said about 93 per cent of the work had been completed by October 2023 and that the state government issued a Substantial Completion Certificate in November 2024.

However, disagreements later arose over claims involving extensions of time, price adjustments and increased costs of materials and labour, eventually leading to arbitration.

Gamji Nigeria Company Limited said an arbitral panel issued a final award on 24 July 2026, directing the Osun government to pay $13.9 million and N157.5 million in reimbursable arbitration fees, with 20 per cent annual interest on any outstanding balance after the compliance deadline.

Gamji subsequently approached the Federal High Court after, according to its case, the 24 August deadline for compliance expired without payment.

The Osun government, however, disputes the validity of the award and the manner in which the arbitration was conducted.

Mr Alimi said the state government was denied what it described as “fair hearing and full participation” in the arbitration process.

He said the proceedings and the eventual award were characterised by “several irregularities”, which the state has now challenged before the Lagos State High Court.

The commissioner also disputed the date and existence of an award referenced in the Federal High Court proceedings, saying there was no arbitral award against the state in July 2024 as claimed by Gamji.

“The only Arbitral Award against the State Government was in July, 2026 and the said Award is presently being challenged before the Lagos State High Court by the State Government’s legal team,” Mr Alimi said.

World.title: 2027: Adewale Ayuba backs Tinubu’s re-election, gives reason
World.content:
Nigerian Fuji musician Adewale Ayuba has endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s bid for a second term, saying the president deserves another four years to consolidate his administration’s achievements.

Ayuba, popularly known as Mr Johnson, made his position known in a video shared by Goldmyne TV on Instagram on Sunday.

The singer pointed to what he described as noticeable infrastructure development across the country under Mr Tinubu’s administration.

He said the changes were particularly evident in his hometown, Ikenné, Ogun State, which he used as a personal reference point to assess the impact of the president’s policies.

According to Ayuba, Mr Tinubu should be allowed to complete the projects and initiatives his administration has started.

“I know when I see the good news, I know when good things are happening in my nation. So I travel far and near in Nigeria, and now if I’m going to my town, Ikenne Remo, it takes me only 25 to 30 minutes. And I have five different roads to take to get to Ikenne.

“Not like before, that I had to take the Ibadan Expressway. If I want to go through Ikorodu, I will get to Ikenne. If I want to go through Epe, I will get to Ikenne,” said the singer.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“A second term”

Ayuba said his journey to his hometown was particularly difficult before the Tinubu administration came into power, adding that the deplorable roads also caused significant damage to his car.

He said any leader who delivers tangible results should be given enough time to see their projects through.

Ayuba noted, “And I’m promising you my car will not even go inside the gallop till I reach Ikenné. Any president that is doing that, my brother, we have to allow that kind of president to continue to finish his work.”

Expose

Ayuba also said his travels across various states had allowed him to see the situation in the country for himself.

He said what he has witnessed during these trips compelled him to speak out.

“Anyway, I don’t know what people are thinking about, but somebody wants to come back to finish his eight years, and they want to bring in another president.

“But to me, Adewale Ayuba, what I see is what I’m talking about. I’ve been a musician for ages, and I travel a lot in the state of Nigeria.”

Backstory

Ayuba’s endorsement of Mr Tinubu comes as a growing number of entertainers, including Remi Surutu, Adams “Lege Miami” Kehinde, Yomi Fash-Lanso, Yul Edochie, Seyi Law, Eniola Badmus and Zack Orji, publicly declared their support for the president’s bid for a second term in 2027.

Some of the entertainers also formed EKO57, a political support group created to rally Nigerians behind Mr Tinubu’s re-election. They said the president had performed well since taking office.

The group argued that several of the problems facing the country predated Mr Tinubu’s administration, blaming some of them on the actions and attitudes of Nigerians.

They also claimed that the president had handled several sensitive issues away from public attention, preventing them from escalating.

According to the entertainers, Mr Tinubu’s interventions had helped avert what could otherwise have developed into a more severe crisis.

Mr Tinubu faces a stern re-election bid next year as the country battles with its worst cost-of-living crisis in a generation, brought about by government policies which the president says are essential.

World.title: Nigerians react as PREMIUM TIMES exposes fake professor who regularly features on TV
World.content:
The PREMIUM TIMES investigation exposing Anthony Kila, the pro-chancellor of Michael and Cecilia Ibru University (MCIU), as a fake professor has triggered a barrage of reactions from Nigerians on social media.

For years, Mr Kila was presented as a professor and “Jean Monnet professor” in television and newspaper interviews.

His profiles on the websites of MCIU and the Commonwealth Institute of Advanced and Professional Studies (CIAPS) also identified him as a professor.

But a PREMIUM TIMES investigation published on Saturday found that no recognised academic institution had awarded Mr Kila a professorial title.

The Investigation

Mr Kila claimed that the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies (ECAPS), which he said was based in Cambridge, United Kingdom, awarded him the professorship in 2016. However, the newspaper found no evidence that the institution exists.

The newspaper also reported that the European Education and Culture Executive Agency, which administers the European Union’s Jean Monnet programme, said Mr Kila did not appear as a Jean Monnet project coordinator in its directory.

The investigation also found that Mr Kila’s Google Scholar profile contained 22 works, nine of which PREMIUM TIMES found were not authored by him. Of the works attributed to him, the newspaper said it could not independently establish any as peer-reviewed articles in reputable academic journals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reactions

The investigation has garnered thousands of likes, comments and reshares on the newspaper’s social media pages, including Facebook, Instagram and X.

Nigerians who read the story expressed shock that media organisations could have repeatedly presented Mr Kila as a professor for years without anyone scrutinising his profile.

Some comments commended the newspaper and called for an investigation into more individuals parading fake certificates.

“Wow! The famous Professor Kila on Arise TV. This is someone who talks down on our university system on the Morning Show. He should be prosecuted for false identity and academic fraud,” Yusuf Ali, @EduBeyondHL, wrote on X.

“Nice work, Premium Times,” @IKENNA_911 wrote. “I had to check his Google Scholar profile. All of the work attached to his name, aside from 2 books in Italian, is as recent as 2019-2022. His major work attributed to him is believed to be this other kila (Kikelomo Kila).”

“The craze for titles everywhere,” Joshua Egbodo, another social media user, commented.

Another commenter praised PREMIUM TIMES for investigating Mr Kila and suggested that other people who present themselves as professors should also have their credentials scrutinised.

READ ALSO: Adeboye prayed for him at private meeting after thanksgiving service

Other reactions focused on the wider issue of people presenting questionable academic credentials in Nigeria.

“Even though he speaks beautifully, he scarcely connects the dots in his analysis. If you listened intelligently, you would understand what I mean. The phonetics covers a lot of holes…,” wrote @Bodexus1

“I am shocked. Such an intelligent man could be mixed up with embellishments like this. Very articulate person. Kudos @PremiumTimesng,” @oluseyelawrence, posted.

“Interestingly, he may not be the only one caught in this web of deceit. My sense, and very certainly, too, there are many more who attained professorship in the country through one opaque means or another. NUC needs to wake up from its snoring slumber and do due diligence in cleaning this disgusting, messy, and unfortunate uprising in the academic environment,” another person, @drbak_, posted.

World.title: Who’s going to win BBNaija Season 11?
World.content:
After more than 70 days of drama, strategy, romance, task victories, nominations and unexpected twists, Big Brother Naija Season 11, “Show Ya Sef”, reaches its climax tonight, Sunday, 4 October.

The grand finale begins at 7pm WAT, with nine housemates still in contention for the ₦160 million prize package.

The season opened on 26 July with 24 housemates. Still, a series of evictions, twists and a disqualification have reduced the field to Aikou, Barry, Bluethopia, Flora, Oyin, Ricky, Sheba, Temi Nkem and Tram.

Voting closed on Friday, 2 October, leaving viewers with one final question: Who has done enough to win?

A season of twists

“Show Ya Sef” introduced one of its biggest twists from the opening weeks with the Gambit.

Aikou and Flora were selected as Gambits, guaranteeing them a place in the finale while initially preventing them from competing for the grand prize.

The arrangement gave them a major advantage as other housemates battled through nominations and evictions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

That changed in Week Six when the Gambit status ended and both housemates returned to the main competition, making them eligible to win the prize.

By then, several contestants had already left.

Martins and Mercedes were evicted in Week Two, followed by Kamsy in Week Three and Cassi in Week Four. Sultex and Goddessa departed in a double eviction in Week Five, while Gerard left in Week Six.

The competition became even more unpredictable in Week Seven when Nomy was disqualified following repeated rule violations. Abi and Araga were also evicted that week.

Then came Barry’s defining moment.

Big move

Barry won the Week Eight Head of House challenge and secured the Ultimate Veto Power.

Rather than using the advantage solely for himself, he chose “Immunity For All”, cancelling the planned eviction and protecting the housemates from elimination.

The move made Barry one of the season’s most influential players and helped take 10 housemates into the final stage of the competition.

Barry later won the final Head of House challenge, becoming a two-time HoH winner.

But the final group suffered another major change when Keivo was disqualified on 29 September after a physical confrontation with Tram.

His exit reduced the field to nine.

Final nine

Aikou

Aikou’s journey is arguably the most unusual.

He began the season as a Gambit, operating under special conditions before eventually becoming a regular competitor.

Known as the “Professor”, Aikou has built his game around intelligence, humour, relationships and thoughtful conversations rather than constant confrontation.

His ability to adapt after the Gambit ended strengthened his case, while Barry’s decision to save him with the Ultimate Veto further demonstrated his importance in the house.

Aikou’s biggest advantage is that he has remained distinctive without depending entirely on drama.

Temi Nkem

Temi Nkem has been one of the season’s most visible housemates.

Bold, outspoken and expressive, she has consistently remained part of the major conversations in the house.

Her journey has included confrontations, friendships, emotional moments and romantic storylines, while her personality has made her one of the easiest finalists for viewers to identify.

She has also shown a strong understanding of the entertainment side of the game.

That visibility could be her biggest weapon tonight.

Barry

Barry has perhaps the strongest case for game impact.

He won two Head of House titles, became the first housemate to secure a place in the finale and controlled the Ultimate Veto.

His “Immunity For All” decision was one of the season’s biggest strategic moves and directly influenced the final stages of the competition.

However, winning challenges does not automatically guarantee public support.

Barry’s chances will depend on whether viewers value his strategic influence as much as his competitors’ personalities.

Sheba

Sheba has built a strong all-round case for the crown.

She was an early Head of House and has remained competitive in tasks while maintaining a strong presence in the house.

Her confidence, communication skills and leadership qualities have kept her relevant without relying on one major storyline.

She may not have generated as much noise as Temi Nkem, but her consistency could work in her favour with voters looking for a complete player.

Tram

Tram entered the house focused on competition rather than romance or unnecessary distractions.

He eventually became Head of House in Week Seven and survived several difficult stages of the competition.

His biggest late-season storyline involved his confrontation with Keivo, which eventually resulted in Keivo’s disqualification.

Tram’s strongest argument is resilience. He has repeatedly survived moments that could have ended his journey.

Bluethopia

Bluethopia has brought energy, humour and strong personality to the competition.

She has developed friendships and featured in some of the season’s relationship-driven storylines.

Her visibility has fluctuated, but she has kept surviving.

To win, however, her supporters will need to turn that entertainment value into a strong final voting push.

Flora

Flora’s journey has been defined by adaptation.

She started the season as a Gambit alongside Aikou before becoming eligible to compete for the prize.

Her cooking, personality and relationships helped maintain her relevance after the twist ended.

Reaching the final nine after losing the protection she started with is one of the strongest parts of her story.

Oyin

Oyin has maintained a steady presence throughout the competition.

She has been outspoken and creative in house activities and surviving nomination pressure.

Unlike some finalists, she hasn’t had one dominant storyline, but her consistency has kept her in the race.

Ricky

Ricky has played a quieter game focused on relationships, survival and longevity.

His experience has given him a different perspective in the house, while his playful connection with Sheba became one of his more visible storylines.

His challenge is competing against finalists with stronger individual narratives.

Who has the edge?

The final race appears to come down to four major factors: visibility, strategy, consistency and fan mobilisation.

Temi Nkem has the strongest argument on visibility.

Aikou has one of the clearest strategic and character-driven journeys.

Sheba offers perhaps the most balanced overall game.

Barry has had the greatest direct influence on the competition’s structure.

The other finalists can still surprise the field, but their paths to victory seem less clear.

Final prediction

With voting already closed, the finalists can no longer change their positions. The result now depends entirely on the votes already cast.

Based on their journeys, public visibility and apparent momentum, Temi Nkem and Aikou appear to be the strongest contenders.

Temi has the personality, entertainment value, and visibility to drive a public vote.

Aikou, meanwhile, has built a more strategic and cerebral identity while maintaining strong relationships and surviving the unusual Gambit twist.

Sheba remains a serious threat, particularly because of her consistency and leadership. At the same time, Barry is the strongest dark horse after his two HoH victories and decisive use of the Ultimate Veto.

The peak contest is now between Aikou and Temi.

PREMIUM TIMES’s top four are Temi Nkem, Aikou, Sheba, and Barry. We, however, tip Aikou to win the competition this year.

But BBNaija has repeatedly shown that predictions can collapse once the final votes are counted.

After more than 70 days of “Show Ya Sef”, the housemates have done everything they can.

Tonight, the public has the final say.

At 7pm WAT, the nine finalists will return to the stage as Ebuka Obi-Uchendu hosts the grand finale.

One by one, the finalists will leave the stage until only one remains.

That housemate will become the winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11 and take the crown from the Season 10 winner, Imisi.

World.title: ‘We are already making corrections’: Akor Adams backs Super Eagles to restore standards after Bissau setback
World.content:
Super Eagles forward Akor Adams says the team has begun addressing the shortcomings exposed by their 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau, and he expressed confidence that Nigeria can rediscover its high standards.

Adams acknowledged that the result was disappointing, particularly given the importance of the encounter to Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Still, they insisted that the players had accepted responsibility for their performance.

Speaking to the Super Eagles media team ahead of Tuesday’s international friendly against Russia, the forward said the team was already working to ensure that the setback does not become a recurring problem.

“I think there are many factors that happen in the game, but it’s not a game we should lose, which we would take responsibility for, and we have taken responsibility for that,” he said.

“It’s a game we prepared very well for. We know how important it was to us in the qualification phase. But looking back, we are already making corrections to what happened in the game.”

Nigeria began their Group L campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo. Still, it suffered a heavy defeat in Bissau on 29 September, leaving the team with work to do as the qualifiers progress.

The loss also prompted coach Éric Chelle to acknowledge that Guinea-Bissau played with more aggression and intensity, while Nigeria struggled to find solutions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Adams said the Super Eagles understood the expectations attached to the national team and must now demonstrate that they can consistently meet them.

“We already set the standards very high, so living up to that standard is what we wake up to do every day as the Super Eagles. And, yeah, for me, that’s one thing we should do going into the next games. We are aware of the standards, and we should live up to that,” he said.

No excuses for defeat

The forward also addressed the difficult playing conditions in Guinea-Bissau, arguing that better pitches should be a basic requirement for African football.

However, he stressed that the circumstances surrounding a match could not absolve professionals of their responsibility to deliver.

“I think a good pitch should be a bare minimum for African football. We all know this, and I’m not making any excuses. I would not make excuses. We are professionals; we should know that there are a lot of things that come with the game — the weather, the referee, whatever the circumstance. We should be able to find our way,” he said.

Adams said the defeat left several players devastated, especially given the fixture’s significance and the long journey home without a positive result.

He also understood captain Wilfred Ndidi’s frustration, whose reaction reflected the mood within the squad.

“Yeah, the captain was pissed at us, and I can understand from his point of view. Many of the boys were not happy, completely devastated, coming away after a long trip and not taking anything back home in an important qualification game,” he said.

Adams admitted Nigeria had hoped to avoid a situation where their qualification hopes would depend on other teams’ results.

“With qualifications, we try our best in this generation not to be in a place where we need another team to either do good or do bad so we qualify. But we fell short against Bissau, and we understand better now,” he said.

Russia test

The Super Eagles will have a chance to respond when they face Russia in Moscow on Tuesday.

Adams said the friendly would be important for the entire squad, including new players and those hoping to make their senior international debuts.

He welcomed the newcomers but emphasised that the expectations of representing Nigeria remain unchanged.

“It’s still the Super Eagles, and we know what we stand for. The coach has made it clear that we are here to try our best to win. Russia is a very good team as well, and I think they’re very hungry to play games because of their peculiar situation. For us, it’s to give our best,” he said.

Nigeria and Russia last met in June 2025, when they drew 1-1 in Moscow. Tolu Arokodare scored Nigeria’s equaliser after Semi Ajayi’s own goal had given the hosts the lead.

With supporters expecting a response after the Bissau setback, Adams said the players were conscious of the responsibility to deliver both a positive result and an improved performance.

“I know Nigerians are watching. They love football a lot, and they love the Super Eagles a lot. And, yeah, come out with a good result and also a good performance.”

World.title: Adeboye prayed for him at private meeting after thanksgiving service
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), says the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Enoch Adeboye, prayed for him and expressed confidence in his triumph.

Mr Sowore said this in a Facebook post on Sunday after attending the RCCG’s National Thanksgiving Service at its headquarters in Ebute Metta, Lagos.

The AAC presidential candidate, who said he attended the service on invitation, disclosed that he was accompanied by his party’s National Chairman, Samuel Ajeigbe.

Mr Sowore explained that he met privately with Mr Adeboye after the service and that the cleric offered to pray for him.

“He stated that he follows my activities religiously, expressed certainty that my path is honorable, and said he is confident of my triumph,” Mr Sowore said.

He noted that it was his second meeting with Mr Adeboye at the same venue.

According to Mr Sowore, their first meeting was in 1996, shortly after he completed his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme, when he was involved in a campaign against campus cultism.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Thirty years later, we met again at the same place,” he said.

Mr Sowore thanked members of the church for their warm reception and Mr Adeboye for the conversation and prayers.

He also said his visit was not intended to promote a political agenda.

The meeting came as Mr Sowore continued his trial before the Federal High Court in Abuja over social media posts in which he called President Bola Tinubu a “criminal” and alleged corruption in Nigeria.

The State Security Service (SSS) is prosecuting him over the posts.

The latest development in the case is a disagreement over whether the SSS Director-General, Tosin Ajayi, should personally appear as a defence witness.

At Friday’s proceedings, Mr Sowore’s lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, renewed the defence’s request for Mr Ajayi to appear in court.

The defence wants the SSS chief to testify about a letter dated 7 September 2025 asking Mr Sowore to retract his posts about Mr Tinubu.

Mr Olumide-Fusika said an SSS official who had earlier testified could not adequately answer questions about the letter because he had acted on Mr Ajayi’s directive.

The defence had earlier withdrawn its application to subpoena Mr Ajayi after the Attorney-General of the Federation, Lateef Fagbemi, appeared in the case in July and opposed the request.

The prosecution has since opposed the demand for Mr Ajayi’s personal appearance.

The judge adjourned the case until 6 October to rule on whether Mr Ajayi should be compelled to appear personally and testify.

World.title: WAEC appoints new Registrar, Head of Nigeria office
World.content:
The West African Examinations Council (WAEC) has appointed Amos Dangut as its new Registrar and Chief Executive Officer, while Suleiman Kum has been named Head of the Nigeria National Office.

Mr Dangut, who previously headed WAEC’s Nigeria National Office, assumed office as Registrar in October 2026, while Mr Kum succeeded him as Head of the Nigeria office.

The appointments were announced in separate statements by WAEC spokesperson, Moyosola Adesina.

According to the council, Mr Dangut succeeds Pateh Bah of The Gambia and will serve a five-year term until September 2031.

WAEC said its International Governing Board ratified Mr Dangut’s appointment at its 74th Annual Meeting held in Accra, Ghana, in March.

As Registrar, he will oversee the council’s operations across its member countries.

Mr Kum, who served in the office of the Head of National Office before his appointment, takes over the Nigeria office following Mr Dangut’s elevation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

About Amos Dangut

Mr Dangut was born on 2 October 1967.

He obtained a Bachelor of Agriculture in Animal Production in 1991, a Master of Science in Animal Science in 1994, a Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Science in 2017 and a Master of Education in Administration and Planning in 2020.

He began his career in education at St Louis College, Jos, in 1994, where he also served as a WAEC examiner before joining the council in 1998.

At WAEC, he served in several capacities, including Assistant Registrar/Subject Officer in the Test Development Division, Head of Examinations Security, Deputy Branch Controller in Uyo and Bauchi, Branch Controller in Yola, Controller of the Post Examinations Department and Zonal Coordinator of the Ikeja Zonal Office.

He served as Deputy Registrar in the office of the Head of National Office between August and October 2023 before becoming Head of the Nigeria National Office on 2 October 2023.

He remained in that position until he was appointed the 14th Registrar of WAEC.

The examination body described Mr Dangut as an experienced test developer and administrator with expertise in test development and administration, branch and zonal office management.

The council said that for more than two decades, he had used information and communications technology to improve processes in test development, post-test activities and test administration.

His career also includes recognition from the Nigeria Examinations Committee for his handling of examination matters between 2000 and 2006. He also received an award for meritorious service from the Ondo State government and Akoko South Local Government during his NYSC service.

About Suleiman Kum

Mr Kum was born on 16 October 1970 in Minna, Niger State, and hails from Langtang North LGA of Plateau State.

He attended Baptist High School, Jos, where he obtained his General Certificate of Education in 1986/1987. He subsequently studied at the University of Agriculture, Makurdi, where he obtained a Bachelor of Agriculture in Animal Production with Second Class Honours, Upper Division, in 1992.

He later obtained a Postgraduate Diploma in Education from the National Open University of Nigeria (NOUN) in 2025 and is currently completing a Master of Education in Educational Administration and Planning at the university.

Mr Kum began his professional career in 1993 during his National Youth Service Corps deployment at the Division of Agricultural Colleges, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, where he served as Head of the Animal Production Unit.

Between 1995 and 1998, he worked at Baptist High School, Jos, where he served in various capacities, including Form Master, Labour Master, classroom teacher and Health Master.

He received the Light and Life Staff Merit Award in 1998.

He joined WAEC on 17 July 1998 as Assistant Registrar II and rose through the ranks to become Senior Deputy Registrar in 2024.

His roles at WAEC have included Head of Examinations Security in Awka, Yola and Makurdi; Branch Controller in Gusau and Kano; Head of the Security Printing Department; Zonal Coordinator in Port Harcourt and Ikeja; Director of Administration; and Senior Deputy Registrar/Test Administration.

Before his latest appointment, he served in the office of the Head of the Nigeria National Office.

WAEC described Mr Kum as an experienced test developer and administrator with expertise in examination security, test administration and branch and zonal office management.

The council said he led several administrative and technological initiatives, including enhanced security features in its printing operations, the introduction of facial-recognition biometric attendance systems and the delivery of achievement tests through computer-based examinations.

World.title: Osun CP deploys tactical team over cult killings
World.content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

Following recent cult-related killings in Osogbo, Osun State capital, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, has deployed the command’s tactical teams to the metropolis to restore normalcy.

The deployment followed a series of shootings allegedly linked to rival cult groups in different parts of the city.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, quoting the commissioner as describing the recent killings as “disturbing and unacceptable.”

According to the statement, a cult clash occurred on October 2, 2026, around the Owo-Eba area of Osogbo, during which two persons identified as Adebayo Taoreed, aka “Small Rugged,” and Oluwaseyi Daniel, aka “OSHA,” were shot dead.

The police said some other persons also sustained gunshot injuries in the incident.

The statement added that on October 4, suspected cultists invaded the Arowomole area of Osogbo, where one Rasak Wahab, aka “Ojo Iku,” was shot.

He was reportedly evacuated to a hospital and was responding to treatment as of Sunday.

Following the incidents, Zungura directed all tactical teams of the command to relocate to the Oke-Baale area and remain there until normalcy was fully restored.

The teams were also directed to conduct intelligence-led raids and operations professionally and within the ambit of the law, targeting identified cult members, criminal hideouts and other locations allegedly linked to criminal activities.

The police said the cases had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for discreet investigation.

Meanwhile, the commissioner directed Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and tactical commanders to intensify patrols, gather actionable intelligence and maintain sustained security presence in identified flashpoints across the metropolis.

Zungura warned cultists and their sponsors that the state would not be a safe haven for criminals involved in shootings and killings.

He, however, assured residents that the command was in control of the security situation and urged them to continue their lawful activities without fear.

World.title: Kidnapped NYSC members still in captivity
World.content:
…Police locate abductors’ camp, fear IEDs

By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — Prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha highway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, are still in captivity, as security agencies intensify efforts to rescue them.

The victims were among passengers travelling in two buses from Ibadan, Oyo State, to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, and Bende, Abia State, respectively, when armed men attacked the vehicles at Umunoha.

The Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, said security agencies had located the hideout where the abducted prospective corps members were being held, but were exercising caution because the area was reportedly heavily mined with improvised explosive devices (IEDs).

Bosso said security personnel had been following leads and acting on intelligence while combing bushes around the scene of the attack.

He added that a surveillance drone had also been deployed as part of the operation.

The police commissioner said, “Reliable intelligence indicates that the area around the camp of the gunmen, where the corps members are being held, is heavily mined with Improvised Explosive Devices.”

He assured that security operatives were aware of the location of the abductors and their captives, adding that arrangements were being made to deploy a specialised heavy-duty armoured vehicle to breach and penetrate the camp.

The abduction occurred on October 1 along the Umunoha axis of the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway.

In his initial statement on the incident, the Imo State Police Public Relations Officer, Mr Henry Okoye, said the Commissioner of Police, in collaboration with sister security agencies, had deployed tactical teams and operational assets to rescue the abducted corps members and other passengers and apprehend the suspected abductors.

Okoye said two buses involved in the incident had been recovered, while 10 victims were rescued at the scene.

He added that the exact number of persons abducted was being verified at the time and would be made public once confirmed.

“Operatives are conducting coordinated search-and-rescue operations, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects,” Okoye said.

He further said the affected section of the expressway had been reopened and traffic restored, while security personnel remained deployed to protect commuters.

In a subsequent update, the Force Public Relations Officer, Force Headquarters, Mr Aniette Iniedu, said the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, had deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, to Imo State to provide operational direction for the search-and-rescue operation.

According to Iniedu, Nadada arrived in the state with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing operations.

He said the DIG reviewed the deployment of personnel and operational assets and issued further directives to strengthen the coordinated response.

“The search-and-rescue operation has been further intensified, with additional deployments of tactical teams and operational assets across identified areas, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects,” Iniedu said.

The development comes amid varying reports on social media about the fate of the abducted prospective corps members.

However, the latest position attributed to the state police command is that security agencies have established the location of the captives and are working on a strategy to safely access the camp.

The police have not disclosed the exact number of prospective corps members still in captivity.

World.title: Nigeria owes women economy worthy of their labour – Shettima
World.content:
VP Shettima

—Flags off Community Investment Fund to empower business women across Katsina

—Inaugurates several road, public transportation projects, receives decampees into APC fold

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA– THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has advocated for a conducive business environment for Nigerian women to ply their trade, saying the nation owes them an economy worthy of their labour.

He noted that women should be given more space for their ambition to flourish unlike in the past when they carried heavy responsibilities with limited resources for their businesses to thrive.

Senator Shettima stated this on Sunday in Katsina State when he flagged off the Community Investment Fund (CIF) disbursement in a major push for women empowerment and financial inclusion under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up (NFWP-SU) Project at Muhammadu Dikko Stadium, Katsina.

He also inaugurated 32 compressed natural gas-powered buses and 200 electric-powered tricycles under the Katsina State Comprehensive Urban Renewal Programme as well as several completed road projects undertaken to improve traffic flow, connectivity and urban mobility in state metropolis.

The CIF fund disbursement, he said, answers a question that should trouble every government as it borders on how much prosperity has been postponed by asking women to work miracles with too little capital

According to VP Shettima, over 40,000 women in Katsina are eligible to receive business capital after fulfilling the prescribed eligibility conditions and demonstrating satisfactory performance in their savings and group activities.

Making a strong case for women empowerment, he said, “Our daughters should inherit their mothers’ determination without inheriting every obstacle their mothers endured. That is another reason to make this programme succeed. The girl who watches a business grow in her own household learns that skill can yield an income, and that ambition can survive contact with adversity.

“We owe these women an economy worthy of their labour. They have carried heavy responsibilities with limited means; their ambition should now have more room to flourish. With confidence in their abilities, I hereby flag off the Community Investment Fund disbursement under the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up Project in Katsina State. May Almighty Allah bless their efforts and grant our country enduring prosperity.”

The Vice President maintained that the economic reforms of administration of President Bola Tinubu must translate into stronger businesses, greater purchasing power, and an improved quality of life for Nigerians.

His words: “For the administration of His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, economic reform must find expression in the earning capacity of citizens. We must connect national policy to the circumstances of the trader, the producer and the service provider.

“Our task is to make their effort more rewarding, so that the pursuit of national growth becomes intelligible in the accounts of an ordinary household.”

Senator Shettima applauded Governor Dikko Umaru Radda’s sensitivity to what he described as an “economic necessity that reaches beyond the loudest voices,” noting that the governor’s “attention to women and vulnerable households honours an essential duty of leadership: to hear those whose difficulties seldom command a microphone.”

Observing that “a government earns affection when the citizen with the least influence receives its fullest attention, he said, “Katsina’s concern for enterprise acquires deeper meaning when it reaches the woman whose ambitions have remained smaller than her abilities because her resources could carry her no further.

“We should never confuse a small business with a small aspiration. The scale of an enterprise often tells us more about the owner’s access to finance than about the reach of her imagination,” he added.

On the CIF design, VP Shettima said it is an empowerment programme for which training is required, explaining that “money needs knowledge and organisation to produce lasting results.”

He continued: “Through Women Affinity Groups, savings and lending are linked to training, financial literacy and access to productive resources. A woman should understand the terms on which she borrows, distinguish revenue from profit and possess the confidence to question a transaction. Financial participation loses much of its value without informed judgement.

“To the women participating, your savings have spoken for you. Every contribution made despite competing demands records a decision to prepare for tomorrow. Preserve that discipline as your businesses grow. Keep sound records, weigh your purchases carefully and protect the trust within your groups. The habits that qualified you for this investment will matter even more when larger sums pass through your hands.”

The Vice President implored those administering the fund to ensure that eligibility remains the “basis of access, without favouritism or political interference,” pointing out that beneficiaries should understand what they receive and how the process works, while each transaction are properly documented.

Earlier, Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Radda, said the state government has committed an additional N4 billion to the implementation of the Nigeria for Women Programme Scale-Up, bringing the state’s total financial commitment to the programme to N8 billion.

Governor Radda noted that the flag-off of the programme was expanding economic opportunities for women across the state with the ultimate objective of improving their livelihoods.

He particularly applauded the participation of women living with hearing impairment, particularly the formation of affinity groups to enhance inclusion and describing it as one of the most encouraging developments under the programme.

Governor Radda added that the state government would complement the women-focused empowerment initiative with similar interventions targeting men, stressing that empowering both men and women would strengthen household incomes and promote financial independence.

For his part, the World Bank Country Director for Nigeria, Mr Matthew Verghis, said Nigerian women are already making significant contributions across various sectors of the economy and noted that closing gender gaps would require deliberate action.

The World Bank Country Director commended the Federal and Katsina State Governments for identifying the economic needs of women and choosing to address them through empowerment initiatives.

He also called on the private sector, community leaders and traditional institutions to support efforts aimed at expanding economic opportunities for women across the state.

Earlier, Vice President Shettima inaugurated 32 compressed natural gas-powered buses and 200 electric-powered tricycles under the Katsina State Comprehensive Urban Renewal Programme.

The VP also inaugurated several completed road projects undertaken to improve traffic flow, connectivity and urban mobility in Katsina metropolis.

He also witnessed the reception of prominent political decampees into the All Progressives Congress, APC led by former Secretary to the Katsina State Government, Dr Mustapha Inuwa and other stalwarts including 8 National Assembly aspirants, 18 State House of Assembly aspirants and several political leaders from opposition parties.

World.title: NGE demands 50% presidential threshold, faster election cases
World.content:
Eze Anaba, President, the Nigerian Guild of Editors

…Calls for INEC appointment reforms, independent candidacy

The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called for far-reaching constitutional and electoral reforms, including a 50 per cent threshold for presidential elections and the resolution of electoral disputes before the swearing-in of declared winners.

The Guild also called for reforms to the appointment processes for the Chairman, National Commissioners and Resident Electoral Commissioners of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), as well as State Electoral Commissioners.

The resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued at the end of the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC 2026), held in Enugu from September 24 to 26, 2026.

The communiqué was signed by the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh.

The conference, themed, “The Ballot, the Media and the Task of Keeping Democracy Alive,” was chaired by the Obi of Onitsha, His Royal Majesty Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, while the Archbishop Emeritus of Abuja, His Eminence John Cardinal Onaiyekan, delivered the keynote address.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima participated virtually as Special Guest of Honour, while Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, was the Chief Host.

More than 500 editors, publishers and senior media practitioners from print, broadcast and digital platforms, as well as political, traditional, religious, academic, regulatory and development-sector leaders, attended the conference.

The Guild said the conference examined challenges confronting Nigeria’s electoral democracy, particularly the threats posed by artificial intelligence, misinformation, disinformation, electoral insecurity and declining public confidence in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to the communiqué, the ballot remained the principal instrument through which citizens exercised their sovereign will, but its value depended on credible information, public confidence in the electoral process and the assurance that votes would be properly counted and respected.

The editors identified voter apathy as being influenced by factors including poor governance, electoral violence and intimidation, administrative shortcomings, declining public confidence and concerns over the relationship between electoral outcomes and subsequent judicial decisions.

The Guild expressed concern over perceptions in some sections of the public that judicial interventions in electoral disputes could displace outcomes recorded at the ballot box.

It, however, stressed the need to respect judicial independence while calling for electoral adjudication that is timely, transparent, predictable and impartial, with genuine electoral irregularities appropriately addressed.

The editors called for electoral disputes to be resolved within appropriate timelines, preferably before the swearing-in of declared winners.

They also recommended consideration of a constitutional threshold requiring a presidential candidate to secure up to 50 per cent of votes cast, with a run-off where no candidate meets the threshold.

The Guild further called for a review of restrictions on ordinary voters seeking to challenge electoral results and advocated a constitutional framework that would permit independent candidacy.

AI, misinformation

The conference identified generative artificial intelligence, deepfakes, voice cloning and automated networks as major emerging threats to the integrity of electoral information.

It warned that synthetic content could be rapidly produced and distributed in the form of fabricated election results, cloned voices of public officials, forged documents, manipulated result sheets and fake reports attributed to established media organisations.

The editors said the danger extended beyond individual falsehoods to the erosion of public trust when citizens could no longer distinguish authentic information from fabricated content.

The Guild consequently urged newsrooms to institutionalise fact-checking and verification systems and integrate digital verification, deepfake detection and forensic tools into their editorial workflows.

It also reaffirmed the Nigerian Media Code of Election Coverage (Revised 2022), jointly endorsed by the Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria, Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria, Nigeria Union of Journalists, Nigerian Guild of Editors, Radio, Television, Theatre and Arts Workers Union and Guild of Corporate Online Publishers.

The NGE urged media organisations to adopt the Code and train journalists and other editorial staff on its provisions ahead of the 2027 elections.

The Guild reaffirmed the responsibility of the media to provide accurate, verified and independent information and scrutinise governments, political parties and other centres of power.

It, however, stressed that media scrutiny should not amount to suppressing legitimate achievements.

The editors called for evidence-based journalism that neither exaggerates failures nor suppresses verified achievements and developments.

The Guild also clarified that editorial neutrality meant impartiality among legitimate political contenders and did not require journalists to remain silent in the face of verified wrongdoing or create false equivalence between established facts and unverified claims.

Election security, journalists

The conference urged governments at all levels to remain transparent and accountable and cooperate with the media in the legitimate exercise of its watchdog role, including scrutiny of public programmes and expenditure.

It also called on government and political actors to guarantee equitable access to media space for government and opposition voices while respecting editorial independence.

The Guild declared that election security must include the safety and protection of journalists covering elections.

It warned that the electoral process could not be fully transparent where journalists were threatened, attacked, obstructed or prevented from independently observing and reporting events.

The NGE therefore called on security agencies and political actors to protect journalists and ensure they could perform their constitutional and professional responsibilities without intimidation.

The editors also urged INEC to sustain nationwide readiness assessments, strengthen technical partnerships for cybersecurity and electoral technology, ensure the technical integrity of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and protect the institutional independence of the electoral commission.

They stressed that all technology deployed in elections must remain subject to human oversight, transparency, accountability and legal verification.

‘Inform, Don’t Amplify’

The conference also addressed the challenge of reporting terrorism, acknowledging the balance between the public’s right to know about terrorist attacks and the risk that irresponsible reporting could inadvertently amplify terrorist propaganda, aid recruitment, compromise security operations or traumatise victims.

It consequently endorsed the principle: “Inform, Don’t Amplify.”

The Guild urged newsrooms to identify terrorist claims clearly as claims until independently verified and avoid reproducing propaganda, recruitment messages, slogans or graphic material except where there was compelling editorial justification.

It resolved that acts of terrorism should be reported responsibly and accurately without giving undue publicity or oxygen to terrorist organisations or inadvertently encouraging further acts of violence.

The conference reaffirmed that the media should remain “pro-Nigeria, pro-Ballot and pro-People”, rather than align itself with any political party.

It stressed that the credibility of Nigeria’s democracy ultimately depended on an electoral process in which citizens could make informed choices, cast their votes freely and have confidence that their votes would be accurately counted and respected.

Among the major papers presented at the conference were those by former Nigerian Bar Association President, Mazi Afam Osigwe, SAN; Professor Auwalu H. Yadudu of Bayero University, Kano; former Managing Director/Editor-in-Chief of The Guardian Newspapers, Martin Oloja; Professor Chinyere Stella Okunna of Paul University, Awka; Professor Farooq A. Kperogi of Kennesaw State University, Georgia, United States; and Dr Richard Okoye, Founder/Chief Medical Director of Save a Life Hospital.

The Guild expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Enugu State for their hospitality and support, as well as speakers, presenters, panellists, sponsors and development partners whose contributions enriched the conference..

World.title: Sanwo-Olu, Adeboye urge Nigerians to serve nation
World.content:
…Sowore seeks peace, progress as Nigeria marks 66th Independence

By Olayinka Latona

LAGOS — Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, and the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, have urged Nigerians to embrace patriotism, responsible leadership and genuine service to God and humanity as the country marks its 66th Independence anniversary.

They spoke at the annual Independence Thanksgiving Service of the RCCG, themed “Acceptable Service,” held at the church’s National Headquarters, The Throne of Grace, Ebute-Metta, Lagos.

The service also featured prayers for Nigeria, its leaders and citizens.

Representing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the event, Sanwo-Olu acknowledged the role of prayers in nation-building and commended the Christian community, particularly the RCCG, for its continued efforts towards the spiritual and moral development of the country.

The governor urged Nigerians to uphold patriotism, resilience and determination, saying national development required collective responsibility.

“The Nigeria we want cannot be built by government alone. It requires each of us to play our part, believe in our country, and work together towards a better future,” Sanwo-Olu said.

He added, “I encourage every Lagosian to keep pushing forward and doing their part. Progress comes when we work together and keep faith in our state and our country.”

Sanwo-Olu said the thanksgiving provided an opportunity for Nigerians to reflect on the country’s past, present and the future they collectively desired to build.

He also introduced the APC governorship candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and his running mate to the congregation.

In his sermon, Adeboye charged Nigerians, particularly leaders, to understand the essence of true service, stressing that every individual had a purpose and responsibility to fulfil.

“We are created for service. If you are alive today, it is because God is giving you a little more time—perhaps so that you may begin to serve,” Adeboye said.

He warned against unproductive lives, saying those who claimed to serve God must ensure that their service was driven by the right motives.

According to him, service to God becomes acceptable when it is motivated by a genuine desire to do His will and serve humanity.

“If you know the will of your Master and do not do it, such a person is living on borrowed time because they are occupying space that could be given to someone else,” he said.

Adeboye also cautioned that religious activities, including miracles and other spiritual works, did not automatically make a person’s service acceptable if the motive behind them was wrong.

He urged Nigerians to remember the inevitability of divine judgment, saying actions and motives would ultimately be tested.

“Let us remember the day of judgment. We can pretend that we are serving God, that we are doing everything He wants us to do for His people, but you cannot deceive God,” he said.

Adeboye illustrated his message with the functions of different parts of the human body, saying each was created for a specific purpose.

He said the hands, legs, eyes and mouth were designed for productive purposes, while cautioning against using the mouth for gossip and other negative activities.

Also at the service was the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, who called for peace, progress and greater national cohesion.

Sowore said Nigerians should appreciate the relative peace in the country and work together across religious lines to promote national development.

“It is important that everybody in the country should appreciate the fact that we are still experiencing some kind of peace, but we all really need peace and progress in the country.

“We are also ready to work with everybody, whether Muslim or Christian,” he said.

The service featured dedicated prayers for Nigeria led by Pastor Foluke Adeboye, wife of the RCCG General Overseer.

She prayed for God’s mercy and forgiveness of the nation’s sins, as well as wisdom for leaders and divine intervention in the affairs of the country.
