World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced an increase on Sunday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,580.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,579.5 Iraqi dinars on Sunday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,585 Iraqi dinars and 1,575 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate increased, fluctuating between 1,580.5 and 1,580 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars for every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq probes US flag desecration during Sovereignty Day parade
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Sunday the formation of an investigative committee in response to an incident in which a US flag was desecrated during the recent parade marking the Sovereignty Day in Baghdad.

The spokesperson for the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Sabah al-Numan, confirmed that the individuals involved in the incident had already been arrested.

According to reports, military vehicles of Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) were filmed driving over large US and Israeli flags laid across the roadway during parade processions marking “Sovereignty Day,” which commemorates the end of the US-led international coalition’s mission in Iraq.

The footage gained international attention after US Congressman Joe Wilson shared it on social media, publicly criticizing Iraq’s state sovereignty.

Al-Zaidi, as commander-in-chief, strongly denounced the crime, highlighting the legal and diplomatic need to respect friendly countries’ emblems and authorized foreign embassies.

The prime minister urged the committee to conclude its work quickly so that those involved can face legal responsibility under Iraqi law.

World.title: Spy chief Clayton, the Trump loyalist tech bosses trust on AI
World.content:
Washington – Jay Clayton, Donald Trump’s pick for AI czar, is the nation’s top spy, and a rare figure trusted by both the president and the tech bosses determined to keep the AI boom roaring.

The 60-year-old lawyer, who will keep his post as director of national intelligence, is unlikely to question the central place of artificial intelligence in the US economy, even as opposition to the technology grows among American voters.

“Jay Clayton is a golden asset for the administration because he’s so well respected by tech leaders as well as many in the government,” said Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co, an investment company.

“He is not a typical Beltway bureaucrat,” Ives added, calling the appointment “bullish for the industry because you can’t just have a regular political appointee.”

A regular golf partner of Trump, Clayton entered politics when Trump picked him to lead the Securities and Exchange Commission, the national markets regulator, in 2017.

A longtime Wall Street lawyer at Sullivan & Cromwell, where he represented Goldman Sachs during the 2008 financial crisis, Clayton ran the market regulator without ruffling feathers. He brought cases against crypto companies, an industry that has since become closely aligned with Trump and his family.

His wife, Gretchen Butler Clayton, worked as a wealth manager at Goldman Sachs but stepped down when he joined the government in 2017.

– No David Sacks –

Trump picked Clayton to lead the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York at the start of his second term, where he took on cases dear to the president, including a probe ordered by Trump into ties between prominent Democrats and the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

His office also signed off on controversial subpoenas against New York Times reporters days before his confirmation hearing for the intelligence post. The Senate confirmed him in July.

But Clayton is no David Sacks, the Silicon Valley venture capitalist who held the AI role at the start of Trump’s second term.

Clayton has no technology background, but does hold an engineering degree from the University of Pennsylvania, where he also earned his law degree, as well as an economics degree from the University of Cambridge.

“Jay Clayton doesn’t have the same deep background in technology that Sacks brought to the role, but he has a rich federal resume and significant experience navigating the federal bureaucracy,” said Aalok Mehta of the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“He also seems to be highly in sync with the president’s thinking right now — though of course we have seen plenty of examples of other advisors that started out that way but ultimately fell out of favor,” Mehta added.

Carl Tobias, a law professor at the University of Richmond, said juggling two major jobs would be a challenge, though Trump has handed multiple roles to trusted officials in his second term, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

– National security –

“Jay Clayton ultimately is going to have to do what the president wants,” said Connor Martin, a national security fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations.

But by giving the AI portfolio to the nation’s top spy, Trump seemed to be accepting arguments that the technology poses real dangers for cybersecurity and is key to the geopolitical rivalry with China, he added.

A tech industry source in Washington said the industry largely welcomed the appointment, but cautioned against expecting major change.

“Jay Clayton is not going to preside over some big regulatory effort,” the source said. “If he brings coherence to the policy, or provides details that bring clarity, those would be wins.”

Clayton will not be the only voice in Trump’s ear on AI, however.

Sacks, along with tech bosses including Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, will continue to hold significant sway over how the president approaches the industry.

Elon Musk is also back in Trump’s good graces after their falling out in 2025.

Clayton takes on the role days after tech bosses signed a commitment at the White House to self-police their AI models, an accord Trump called “morally binding.”

Mehta said he expected Clayton to coordinate the government more effectively while sticking to Trump’s goal of not slowing the industry.

“But at the same time, the problems he is facing — like around AI safety and sentiment — are bigger and harder now, and they are happening at a much faster clip,” he said.

World.title: Trump confirms national intelligence chief as new AI czar
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump on Sunday confirmed national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as head of a new White House task force on artificial intelligence, amid increasingly vocal warnings from researchers about the technology’s potential dangers.

Under Clayton, the new Super Intelligence Force — Trump’s preferred term for artificial intelligence — will ensure that the United States “continue to lead the world” in AI development, the president posted on his Truth Social platform.

Trump said the force had also been tasked to “protect the interests, and improve the lives of all Americans.”

Clayton will become the second person to hold the informal title after venture capitalist David Sacks, who held the role at the start of Trump’s second term before stepping down.

Sacks continues to advise the president on AI, as does Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

Trump said last month he would create an AI force modeled on the Space Force he established during his first term, and name a czar to coordinate federal efforts.

A longtime Wall Street lawyer, Clayton represented Goldman Sachs during the 2008 financial crisis and Barclays in its purchase of Lehman Brothers’ assets.

He chaired the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump’s first term, where he largely took a pro-business stance but brought enforcement cases against the nascent crypto industry.

Crypto entrepreneurs have since become major Trump backers.

Trump tapped Clayton to lead federal prosecutors in Manhattan at the start of his second term, and the Senate confirmed him as intelligence chief in July.

He has no background in the tech industry.

The appointment would come as AI researchers warn of the technology’s potential dangers, following cases of AI systems going rogue and hacking outside systems.

Trump has resisted tighter AI regulation, arguing a slowdown could hand Chinese firms an advantage and that federal law enforcement can deal with bad actors misusing the technology.

Tech bosses at a White House meeting this week signed a commitment to self-police AI, an accord Trump described as “morally binding.”

Attitudes toward AI have soured in Washington, with lawmakers increasingly under pressure from voters to curb or slow its development over fears it could displace workers and upend society.

Those concerns gained force from a run of incidents in which tech giant OpenAI’s autonomous systems slipped out of their constraints, beginning with a July breach of Hugging Face — a widely used platform for sharing AI models.

Clayton told the Wall Street Journal on Saturday that Trump had insisted the new task force ensure US primacy in the AI field, amid stiff competition from China.

“The risk of not being first is high,” Clayton told the Journal.

“Not being first increases the identified, and unidentified, risks, particularly from our adversaries. Being first will better enable us to address those risks on behalf of the American people.”

World.title: Iraq’s financial revenues hit $30 billion in seven months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Finance revealed on Sunday that the country’s total revenues reached approximately 39.09 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $30 billion) until the end of July 2026, with oil revenues accounting for about 78 percent of total state resources.

The revenues from oil exports totaled over 30.35 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $23.24 billion). In comparison, non-oil revenues amounted to 8.74 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $6.7 billion), which represented about 22 percent of the total income.

The figures indicated that total revenues of 39.09 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30 billion) were offset by total expenditures of approximately 65.42 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $50.09 billion), resulting in a deficit of 26.32 trillion Iraqi dinars ($20.15 billion).

Iraq’s financial revenues between January and April surpassed 31.16 trillion Iraqi dinars ($23.6 billion).

Oil sales during the first four months of 2026 produced 26.12 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $19.9 billion), accounting for 84 percent of overall state income, while non-oil revenues were around 5.04 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $3.84 billion).

Iraq’s significant reliance on oil as the primary source of its national budget exposes the country to vulnerabilities stemming from global crises that impact the oil sector.

The government’s reliance on oil to address the deficit forces it to seek external or internal loans, underscoring its struggle to manage public finances efficiently and revealing a deficiency in developing alternative revenue streams.

World.title: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war
World.content:
Tehran – Iran’s top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States’ war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

The main point of contention remains Iran’s attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.

“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.

“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” he continued, adding “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.

The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.

Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.

The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.

On Sunday, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz “reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room”, though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.

The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel’s origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.

– Focused on Hormuz –

Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.

Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.

Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being “in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues”.

“We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said, adding that reopening the waterway required “an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions”.

The United States and Israel have characterised the war as being necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons — a goal it has long denied pursuing — though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.

The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region.

US media outlet Axios reported that Washington has deployed additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to help protect key energy facilities from possible Iranian retaliation.

It also reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group were heading to the Middle East, where they could join two other US carrier strike groups already in the region.

Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Russia strikes hit Kyiv as Germany’s Merz visits
World.content:
Kyiv – Russia struck another major bridge in Kyiv on Sunday, soon after Germany’s chancellor arrived on a surprise visit to show European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks.

Air raid sirens blared repeatedly across the Ukrainian capital throughout the morning, including as Friedrich Merz met President Volodymyr Zelensky at the National Academy of Sciences, which was hit by a Russian attack drone on Tuesday.

Zelensky told him that people in Kyiv were suffering “terrible nights and days” from the relentless attacks, and called Ukraine’s Russian adversaries “absolute barbarians”.

“We can see the entire pointlessness of this war at this place,” noted Merz.

“These barbarous attacks on the civilian population of Ukraine must stop. These are war crimes that are being committed daily here.”

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said a strike had damaged the road surface on the Northern Bridge — one of several connecting the eastern and western parts of the city over the Dnipro river which have been struck in recent days.

Images posted on messaging channels appeared to show a missile slamming into the structure, sending up a fireball as traffic crossed.

Klitschko has said that Kyiv — largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontlines in nearly five years of conflict — should now be on a war footing due to the upsurge in attacks.

A spate of round-the-clock attacks has hit residential areas, petrol stations, schools, rail and communications infrastructure while near-constant air raid sirens disrupt daily life and put people on edge.

Merz said as he arrived that Ukraine “needs all our support in the coming weeks”.

“If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us,” he added.

Ukraine wants more Western military support, including advanced interceptors to shoot down Russia’s new fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

On Sunday, Zelensky promised “important agreements”. Government sources in Berlin said they were expected to shake hands on a new package of military support worth more than $1 billion.

It includes combat drones and satellite technology to help Ukraine hit Russian launch sites, as well as for the joint production of anti-jet drones, the German sources said.

“This support addresses the most significant current gap in Ukraine’s air defence system. The impact is expected to be rapid and tangible,” a source said.

– Military support –

Merz this week called for unity against Russia within NATO and the European Union as well as his own country, where the far-right, Moscow-friendly AfD opposition is on the rise.

There have been increasing fears in Europe that it could find itself in Russia’s crosshairs, including from covert attacks, if it is not stopped in Ukraine.

On Saturday, Russia warned foreigners and diplomats to leave Kyiv, saying “massive” new airstrikes would hit the city.

The Russian foreign ministry declared in a statement that “responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning”.

Moscow had issued a similar warning in May, but leaders from countries supporting Ukraine have defied the Russian warnings and continued to make visits.

“The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe’s support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!” EU ambassador Katarina Mathernova wrote on X on Sunday.

Mathernova told AFP separately that “nobody is moving”, although European embassies always had contingency plans, including for winter, she added.

Russia has admitted deliberately targeting Ukraine’s energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to -20C.

In Kyiv, which is home to some three million people, residents have begun mulling what to do if that happens again. The government has also suggested that the vulnerable and disabled should consider leaving.

Merz’s trip was expected to announce some 350 million euros to help provide generators, transformer stations and for grid repairs, German government sources said.

World.title: Iraq, OPEC+ members agree to keep oil production unchanged
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The OPEC+ alliance decided in principle to maintain oil output objectives unchanged during a meeting on Sunday, according to Reuters.

The meeting included seven key OPEC+ members—Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan, and Oman—and took place as Gulf states work to boost exports following months of turmoil caused by the US war against Iran; however, most producers are still pumping much below their goal quotas.

The OPEC+ alliance had raised its production targets for most of the year before deciding to keep them unchanged in October, after completing the phasing out of voluntary cuts, which totaled approximately 1.65 million barrels per day that began in 2023.

OPEC+ comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and its allies, including Russia.

Sources indicated that a review by OPEC+, intended to establish oil production quotas for member states for 2027, has been postponed.

This delay is attributed to the disruption of capacity-expansion initiatives across the Middle East caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which complicates the evaluation of future production capabilities for member states.

World.title: Beyond advocacy: Government steps up diplomatic push for Ukraine settlement
World.content:

External affairs minister S Jaishankar said Sunday India's approach to the Russia-Ukraine war had moved beyond just the advocacy of dialogue and diplomacy between the 2 countries, suggesting India might be looking to actively mediate in the conflict. Both Moscow and Kyiv have said in the past few days that India had come up with ideas and proposals to bring the war to an end.Unlike China and other countries that have looked to mediate, India had so far offered support for all global peace initiatives - advocating engagement between the involved parties - but without introducing any signature proposal. This approach was anchored in its own emphasis on bilateralism in resolving disputes between countries.Offering a teaser about India's proposal, Jaishankar said India is looking to address some immediate concerns that both Russia and Ukraine have on "grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities"."We would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard.We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue," said the minister, speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting here.Jaishankar had himself said during his visit to Ukraine last month â shortly after PM Narendra Modi's message to President Vladimir to stop the "endless war â that India was discussing ideas that could be developed for cessation of hostilities. On Friday, while Putin had announced Modi had very good ideas for peace, Ukraine foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India had come up with the "broadest" peace proposal out of the 4 that it had received from other countries, including the US.This shift in India's position seems driven by the direct domestic fallout of the conflict, whether it's commercial shipping disruptions in the Black Sea or an intense blowback from the US over India's continued purchase of Russian crude.In his remarks â not for the first time â Jaishankar stressed that Russia had stood by India when the latterâs security and territorial integrity was threatened and that Indiaâs current approach to Moscow is shaped by the legacy.âAt a time when much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us (Pakistan), Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and we are shaped in many ways by that legacy,â he said.On the US, Jaishankar said that the world today was marked by a radical repositioning of the US which had deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power" and also the rise of China.âThe current system was significantly underwritten by the United States. That underwriting is diluting. There are gaps which have emerged,â he said.The minister underlined that the sharp competition between the US and China was not limited to these 2 countries alone. "It has led to weaponization of any leverage that any country has. And that competition coexists with the complexity of interdependence," said the minister.

World.title: 'Little bit more involved': Jaishankar says India has 'gone beyond advocacy' to end Russia-Ukraine war

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said that India has stepped beyond traditional advocacy to actively broker peace and operational agreements between Russia and Ukraine.During the Munich leaders meeting, Jaishankar said that India is actively holding conversations with Russia and Ukraine to end the war, which has stretched on for more than four years."Having said that, we are seeing today an unfortunate conflict. World.title: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao: Seven decades, many worlds of cinema
World.content:
BENGALURU:

, who died in Chennai on Saturday aged 95, had a career that spanned more than seven decades of

. He entered films in 1954 as an apprentice to legendary Telugu filmmaker KV Reddy, assisting him on Donga Ramudu and Mayabazar.

From those early days on the sets of a Telugu classic, Rao went on to become one of Indian cinemaâs most inventive filmmakers, leaving a particularly rich mark on Kannada cinema while also making acclaimed films in Tamil, Telugu and other languages.

His Kannada journey began before he became a director. Rao was the executive director of Samskara (1970), Pattabhirama Reddyâs landmark adaptation of UR Ananthamurthyâs novel.

The film, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film, became a defining work of Kannada parallel cinema. It was an early indication of the range of a filmmaker who would later move comfortably between art-house cinema and popular entertainment.

His directorial debut in Kannada came with Rajkumar in Haalu Jenu in 1982. What followed was one of the notable actor-director collaborations in Kannada cinema, with Chalisuva Modagalu, Eradu Nakshatragalu, Shravana Banthu, Jwaalamukhi, Bhagyada Lakshmi Baramma and Devatha Manushya â all after Gogak Chaluvali.





The films moved across family drama, romance, crime and comedy, with Rao adapting his craft to each.

Devatha Manushya was also Rajkumarâs 200th film.

His association with the Rajkumar family extended beyond the thespian himself. In Anand (1986), Rao introduced Shivarajkumar as a leading man. He later directed Raghavendra Rajkumar in Chiranjeevi Sudhakar. His association with the Rajkumar banner also included work on other films produced by the family.

There was another side to Raoâs Kannada work that is less often remembered: music. A disciple of composer S Rajeswara Rao, he also composed music, giving Kannada cinema some memorable albums. He composed the songs and score for Bhagyada Lakshmi Baramma and the songs for Samyuktha, moving between direction and music with the same ease with which he moved between genres.

Then came Pushpaka Vimana (1987), the dialogue-free film starring Kamal Haasan.

The movie, which became one of the most distinctive films of its time, was another example of Rao refusing to be confined by conventional cinematic language. Though often remembered primarily through its Tamil connection, it was produced as a Kannada entry and won the National Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment.

His apprenticeship under KV Reddy had taken him through some of Telugu cinemaâs landmark films.

Decades later, he returned to Telugu cinema as a director with films such as Aditya 369 and Bhairava Dweepam. In Tamil, his collaborations with Kamal Haasan produced films including Raja Paarvai, Apoorva Sagodharargal and Michael Madana Kama Rajan. His work also extended to Hindi, Malayalam and English.

Across more than seven decades, Raoâs filmography was less a straight line than a series of departures. He began as a young apprentice learning from KV Reddy on films such as Mayabazar, became part of the Kannada New Wave through Samskara, worked extensively with Rajkumar, introduced two of his sons, experimented with a dialogue-free film and continued moving between languages and genres almost until the end.

World.title: Mumbai Police registers FIR against organisers of Thackerays' anti-SIR march

NEW DELHI:

on Sunday registered an FIR against the organisers of the joint morcha led by

and Shiv Sena (UBT) for not obtaining mandatory police clearance and violating prohibitory orders.

The FIR was registered at the Azad Maidan police station after Uddhav Thackeray and Raj Thackeray led a joint protest march towards the BMC headquarters against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Uddhav said the protest was aimed at opposing what he described as an attack on voters' rights and democracy. He claimed that the names of "13 crore people" had been deleted from electoral rolls across the country and alleged that voters had also been excluded in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu.

"We are standing here today to overthrow the dictator," he said.

"Does the home ministry have the power to cancel a person's citizenship rights? They are using that power through Gyanesh Kumar, and that is why we do not want Gyanesh Kumar," he added.

World.title: India successfully demonstrates its first free-space quantum-secure communication link for over 5.5 km
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Indian deep-tech startup QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated Indiaâs first free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) link for over 5.56 km.

A free-space QKD link is an ultra-secure way to share secret digital passwords using particles of light travelling through open air or space instead of a physical fibre-optic cable. It uses quantum mechanics principles, and any attempt by an outsider to intercept or measure the photons changes their state; therefore, it is the most secure form of sending data. Traditional QKD is limited by signal loss inside fibre-optic cables, whereas free-space links allow communication across open terrain, water or obstacles where laying cables is difficult.

Free-space optics form the foundational bridge for transmitting keys between Earth and orbiting satellites and create the backbone for a global, quantum-secure internet network.

âThe field trial, conducted on the night of Sept 27â28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG-N and IIT-G,â the IT and electronics ministry said in a statement on Saturday.

Using QNu Labsâ pointing, acquisition and tracking system, the trial achieved a stable quantum bit error rate below 5% and generated secure keys at a rate of 230â260 bps.





These keys were integrated with BISAG-Nâs post-quantum cryptography-enabled Vedic Kavach platform, enabling successful end-to-end encryption and decryption of test messages.

Vinay Thakur, director general, BISAG-N, said the integration of Vedic Kavach with QNu Labsâ QKD technology marks a significant step towards practical quantum-resilient communication systems. Sunil Gupta, co-founder and CEO, QNu Labs, emphasised that the successful 5.56 km demonstration paves the way for longer-distance quantum-secure networks and satellite-based quantum communication.

The trial provides a foundation for advancing Indiaâs capabilities in secure communication infrastructure, strengthening resilience against emerging quantum-era security threats.

World.title: Ex-Army jawan among 2 held for 'passing' information to Pak on defence movements: Assam CM
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two people, including a retired Army jawan who was later re-employed on a contractual basis, were arrested in Assam for allegedly sharing security-related information with Pakistan, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday.

Sarma said the arrests were made by Assam Police based on inputs from central agencies. âToday, as per input of central agencies, the Assam Police arrested two persons. One is a retired army jawan but currently working on a contractual basis with the army,â he said at a press conference.

âIt has been alleged that they were in touch with Pakistan and were giving information about army movement. We will hand them over to the central agencies,â news agency PTI quoted Sarma saying.

The chief minister said initial reports suggested the two suspects were allegedly honey-trapped by individuals seeking to obtain information from them.

Earlier, Assam Police said its special task force had arrested 31-year-old Abhishek Kumar Singh, a Bihar native living in Guwahati, for alleged espionage activities. Singh, who is from Purba Champaran, was suspected of sharing sensitive information about security forces with a Pakistani intelligence operative (PIO).

World.title: Monthly stipend for senior, junior resident doctors to increase from Rs 75,000 to Rs 1 lakh: Uttarakhand CM
World.content:
Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday announced that stipends for both Senior and Junior Resident doctors in the state have been raised significantly from approximately Rs 75,000 to over Rs 1 lakh per month.

Speaking to the media after the State cabinet meeting in Banbasa, CM Dhami added that around 25-26 decisions were taken during the meeting.

He noted that the deadline for regularising 'Class B' lands in key regions, including Dehradun, Lalkuan, and Bindukhatta, has been extended by one year.

"We have increased the stipends for our Senior and Junior Resident doctors; the amount, which was previously around Rs 75,000, has now been raised to over Rs 1 lakh.

Additionally, we have extended the deadline by one year for the regularisation of 'Class B' lands in areas like Dehradun, Lalkuan, and Bindukhatta. Many other decisions have also been taken, particularly concerning these border regions, totalling around twenty-five or twenty-six decisions," he said.

He added that the Cabinet thoroughly deliberated on managing major state events and seasonal pilgrim traffic.





According to the chief minister, the Cabinet held discussions on ensuring smooth operations, strict travel management, and maintaining optimal road conditions across pilgrim routes amid the ongoing Char Dham Yatra.

"The Char Dham Yatra is currently underway, and we discussed ensuring its smooth management and proper arrangements, including maintaining good road conditions," he said.

He added, "We also deliberated on managing the traffic flow at Kainchi Dham, where the volume of visitors has surged significantly.

Furthermore, we discussed the ongoing 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan."

He emphasised that Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 years of governance on October 7th and programs across all districts will be held to mark the occassion.

Furthermore, the chief minister underlined that the State government is putting efforts in the region based on the vision of an 'Adarsh ââChampawat' (Model Champawat), with all the departments working cohesively here.

"We have initiated efforts to ensure the government reaches even the remote border areas. This region, comprising Banbasa and Tanakpur, falls under the Champawat district, where work is progressing based on the vision of an 'Adarsh ââChampawat' (Model Champawat). All departments are actively working here; the entire Cabinet, along with officials from various departments, has arrived today. This will undoubtedly provide fresh momentum to the region's development and inspire the local people," he said.

Highlighting the military cantonment and BSF deployment, CM Dhami said that the region shares a neighbourly relationship with Nepal, with similar attire, culture, and modes of worship. So, the government has initiated the practice of reaching out to the people before taking major State-level decisions.

"There is a military cantonment here, and a large number of Border Security Force (BSF) personnel are deployed in the area. This is a region bordering Nepal, and we share deep, age-old ties, often described as 'roti-beti' (bonds of food and kinship/marriage) with our neighbours there. We will continue to take significant decisions in the future," he remarked.

World.title: CM Pushkar Singh Dhami chairs first-ever cabinet meeting in Champawat to boost border area development
World.content:
BANBASA: In a new initiative aimed at taking governance to the remote and border areas of Uttarakhand, chief minister

chaired a state cabinet meeting at the NHPC complex in Banbasa, Champawat district, bordering the India-Nepal international border.

This was the first-ever cabinet meeting held in Champawat district, during which several important decisions were taken.

Chief minister Dhami said Cabinet meetings would no longer remain confined to Dehradun and would also be held in different districts across the state. This would provide an opportunity to place local issues, development potential and regional priorities directly before the government. He said the state government was working to reduce the gap between governance and the people and ensure that the benefits of development schemes reach the last mile.

The chief minister said border areas were not merely the geographical boundaries of the state but also an important link in the country's security, culture and development. He said connecting people living in border areas with the mainstream of development was a priority of the state government. Infrastructure, employment, tourism and connectivity in these areas were being further strengthened.

He said holding cabinet meetings in different parts of the state would help the government understand local conditions, public expectations and development needs more closely.





It would also pave the way for effective and prompt decisions on issues specific to particular regions.

During the cabinet meeting in Banbasa, chief minister Dhami and members of his council of ministers were presented with the traditional Farra/Chhantoli, an invaluable symbol of Uttarakhand's rich folk traditions. The traditional shield is associated with the famous Bagwal tradition of Devidhura in Champawat.

World.title: Weekend night bike racing puts Chennai residents, motorists on the edge
World.content:
Residents and motorists in the city are alarmed by the growing number of teenagers taking part in bike racing at night during weekends, posing a serious threat to motorists and other road users.

A section of residents staged a protest at Valluvar Kottam on Saturday night, demanding that the City Traffic Police take stringent action to curb the nuisance. The residents said they were unable to sleep due to the noise caused by the bikes and expressed concern over the danger posed by reckless riding.

The issue came into focus following the death of 21-year-old R. Sri Gugan of Raja Annamalaipuram, who worked as a mechanic. In the early hours of Sunday, Gugan was riding his friend’s bike when he lost control of the vehicle on the flyover on Sardar Patel Road, near IIT-Madras.

The bike crashed into a barricade on the flyover, following which Gugan fell from the flyover and died. The incident has once again highlighted the dangers posed by reckless and high-speed riding on city roads, particularly during the night.

Saturday night fever

More than 100 motorcycles were reportedly involved in racing and performing stunts on arterial roads in Anna Salai, Guindy, Valluvarkottam, Kodambakkam and Anna Nagar on Saturday night.

Videos of youngsters engaged in bike racing and performing stunts have since gone viral on social media, prompting netizens to demand stern action from the City Traffic Police against the groups involved. Road users have also complained that many of the riders either remove their number plates or fold them to make the registration numbers difficult to identify.

S. Ramesh, a resident of Adambakkam, said he was driving along Jawaharlal Nehru Salai near Ashok Pillar on Saturday night when he saw more than 15 motorcycles racing from Guindy towards Vadapalani. “The riders were speeding and racing alongside each other, creating anxiety among other road users. I did not see any police personnel along the stretch,” he said.

T. Purushoth, a resident of Anna Nagar 3rd Avenue, said motorcycle stunts had become a common sight on weekends in recent months, particularly near the food streets late at night. “Youngsters ride rashly in these areas. Those approaching Anna Nagar tend to drive cautiously until the Anna Nagar Arch, where police personnel are stationed. But once they get onto the flyover, some riders begin driving recklessly,” he said.

He added that some riders were also seen performing stunts with the motorcycle’s centre stand engaged, causing sparks to fly as the vehicles moved along the road. According to him, roads behind the food streets in Anna Nagar have become a venue for such activities.

A retired City Police official said enforcement against such violations needed to be stricter. He alleged that policemen were sometimes sympathetic towards violators, particularly underage riders involved in bike racing. He pointed to the action taken by police in Thoothukudi on Saturday, where cases were reportedly registered against the parents of underage riders and the vehicles were impounded.

A senior City Traffic Police officer said the motorcycles involved in racing and stunt riding on Saturday night were being identified. “An action plan is being worked out to put an end to this menace,” the officer said.

World.title: Campaigning for byelection ends in Madurantakam and Dharapuram
World.content:
The high-decibel byelection campaign in the Assembly segments of Madurantakam (SC) in Chengalpattu district and Dharapuram (SC) in Tiruppur district ended on Sunday evening, when leaders and cadres of various political parties made a final push to canvass votes.

The stage is now set for polling on October 6. Both the Assembly segments were declared vacant following the resignation of Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama on May 25. They were elected on AIADMK tickets from Madurantakam and Dharapuram, respectively, and resigned within three weeks of being elected to the House. They switched sides to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and are in the race on behalf of the party.

Unlike recent Assembly byelections in Tamil Nadu, the polls in these two constituencies feature a five-cornered contest. The TVK-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance, the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance and the AIADMK-led National Democratic Alliance are in the fray. The Left front is contesting separately, while the Naam Tamilar Katchi is going it alone.

On the last day of the campaign, TVK president and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay went on a roadshow in Dharapuram, canvassing votes for Ms. Sathyabama. Meanwhile, Minister Aadhav Arjuna and other TVK leaders campaigned for Ms. Kumaravel in Madurantakam. DMK president M.K. Stalin and AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami released video messages, canvassing votes for their respective candidates. Leaders of the Left parties and Naam Tamilar Katchi also concluded their campaigns.

The ruling TVK had deployed almost all Ministers as election in-charges in these two constituencies to oversee election work. Mr. Vijay, who had conducted a relatively limited campaign during the Assembly election, had campaigned extensively in these two segments. He addressed a public meeting in each and held roadshows for several kilometres.

The alliance arithmetic has also changed when compared to the previous election. The Congress, the Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, and the Indian Union Muslim League, which were part of the DMK-led alliance, are now with the TVK-led alliance.

The Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar), which was part of the NDA, is now extending support to the TVK. The AIADMK accused the TVK of engineering the defection of its MLAs. Mr Palaniswami and AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran had campaigned extensively in both constituencies.

PMK’s stance

The Pattali Makkal Katchi, a key constituent of the NDA that has considerable influence in northern and western Tamil Nadu, had decided not to extend support to any alliance.

The DMK also undertook an extensive campaign in both Assembly segments, with former Ministers camping and overseeing the poll work. Mr. Stalin and Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin too have campaigned in both constituencies.

Counting on October 9

A total of 27 candidates are in the fray in Madurantakam, while 22 are in the contest in Dharapuram. Polling will begin at 7 a.m. on October 6 and continue until 6 p.m. Counting of votes will take place on October 9, and the results will be declared.

World.title: Police nab three migrant workers over murder of their co-worker in Velachery
World.content:
The Velachery police on Sunday arrested three men in connection with the murder of their fellow migrant worker from Odisha following a dispute over the online transfer of wages.

The city police said the accused – Qasim and his accomplices Sheriful and Tabir, all from Bihar – were involved in the construction of a house in IOB Colony of Velachery. Ranjan used to transfer their wages to them via UPI.

On Saturday, he was found dead with fatal injuries. The Velachery police sent the body to the Government Royapettah Hospital.

During investigation, it was found that a dispute arose between Qasim and Ranjan after ₹45,000, which was intended to be sent to his mother via UPI, was transferred to a different bank account. Following an argument, Qasim stabbed Ranjan to death.

World.title: Tiruvottiyur residents seek flood-free, pollution-free neighbourhood
World.content:
Residents of Tiruvottiyur sought measures to prevent flooding, curb industrial pollution, provide pattas and basic amenities, and strengthen healthcare and waste management at a public assembly held in the area on Sunday.

The Federation of North Chennai Residents Welfare Associations (FNCRWA) and the Village Coordination Committee organised the ‘Tiruvottiyur Makkal Sangamam’ at the Perundalaivar Kamarajar Mandapam.

Among the demands were the raising and strengthening of both banks of the Buckingham Canal by one metre, measures to prevent industrial wastewater and thermal power plant ash from entering the canal and estuary, deepening and widening the Ennore estuary to facilitate the discharge of Kosasthalaiyar river water into the sea.

Association president T.K Shanmugam also sought expansion of Metrorail to Ennore, completion of the Annamalai Nagar-Wimco railway subway, playgrounds and gymnasiums. A self-certification system was sought for individual houses up to 3,000 sq ft, excluding multi-storey buildings.

They sought action against industries violating pollution control rules, including continuous monitoring of air, water and soil quality and transparent disclosure of the findings. The demands also included regular drinking water supply, underground sewerage connections and integrated stormwater drains.

They also sought pattas for eligible long-term residents of government and temple lands, while protecting water bodies and catchment areas. Sale deeds were sought for those who had paid for houses built by the Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board.

World.title: Fresh meniscus transplantation programme launched
World.content:
Rathi Med Speciality Hospital, Chennai, launched a fresh meniscus allograft transplantation (MAT) programme as part of the Chennai Knee Course 2026 on Sunday (October 4).

The programme was inaugurated by IIT-Madras Director V. Kamakoti and Tamil Nadu Health Secretary Darez Ahamed, IAS.

The programme involves using a healthy meniscus from selected patients undergoing total knee replacement as a fresh graft for patients whose damaged meniscus cannot be repaired or reconstructed.

The hospital said it had received a licence from the Tamil Nadu government to perform fresh meniscus transplantation of the knee ), valid until December 2030.

The programme is led by N. Ragunanthan, Director, Head of Orthopaedics, and Consultant Surgeon of the hospital.

The conference, titled ‘The Meniscus 360° – From Repair to Transplant’, discussed meniscus transplantation and knee preservation.

The hospital also presented its Kinematic Knee Treatment and KPA Knee Preservation 360° approach for knee preservation in suitable patients below 60 years of age.

World.title: FIR filed after IIT-D scholar found injured in Munirka flat dies at AIIMS
World.content:
A First Information Report (FIR) has been registered in connection with the death of an IIT Delhi PhD scholar who passed away at AIIMS on Saturday, more than 45 days after being found unconscious at his rented house in Munirka, police said on Sunday.A First Information Report (FIR) was registered on Sunday into the death of an IIT Delhi PhD scholar at AIIMS on Saturday, weeks after he was found unconscious and injured at his rented house in Munirka on August 18, police said.

The case was booked under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for abetment of suicide, following a complaint by an IIT Delhi security officer.

According to the police, the scholar was found unconscious and injured inside his rented house in Munirka on August 18. The door was locked from inside. Neighbours broke open the door, and the police shifted him to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where he remained under treatment until he succumbed to his injuries on October 3, the police said.

Police clarified that the incident did not take place inside the IIT Delhi campus. According to police, neither the family nor witnesses have raised suspicions or made allegations against anyone following the incident. The police said that the CCTV footage from outside the house confirmed that the scholar was alone inside the house.

The FIR has been registered following the Supreme Court’s directions and further probe is under way, said a police officer.

World.title: Fisherfolk oppose plan to build Secretariat at Foreshore Estate
World.content:
Sunday morning witnessed peaceful protests in villages along the Marina Loop Road, with fishermen hoisting black flags on boats, fish stalls, net mending sheds and homes, to mark their opposition to the new Secretariat.

They demand that the State government return the lands belonging to Srinivasapuram to the village and drop the proposal to construct the Secretariat at Foreshore Estate.

Residents of Srinivasapuram took out a march, carrying black flags through the narrow roads of the hamlet.

“The lands originally belonged to fishermen. They were taken over by the [Tamil Nadu] Housing Board with the promise that we will get homes built on them. But we were cheated. We want those lands to be returned to us,” a fisherman said.

Among their demands is the construction of new houses for 15,000 fishermen and their families living along the Marina Loop Road, as most of their houses were built 40 to 50 years ago.

The fishermen have submitted their demands to the Chief Minister’s Special Cell. “We hope the government will take a positive decision on the issue. Since we are the stakeholders who matter the most, we request the government to appoint someone to listen to our grievances before taking such a major decision. We are holding protests only because nobody has discussed the issue with us,” said fishermen leaders G.R. Vijayan and K. Bharathi.

Fishermen of villages such as Nochikuppam, Bhavanikuppam, Domingkuppam, Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, Mullikuppam/Srinivasapuram, Mullimanagar, Nambikai Nagar, Selvarajpuram and Irudayapuram have planned to hold a series of protests to draw the attention of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to their demands.

World.title: MLA helps father return to Vizag from Abu Dhabi after son drowns
World.content:
The father of 14-year-old Surya Prakash, who drowned at the beach near the IT SEZ in Visakhapatnam, reached the city from Abu Dhabi late on Saturday, after efforts were made to facilitate his return to India.

Surya Prakash’s father, Bhaskar Rao, was working in a company in the UAE. According to the family, the company had initially refused to grant him leave following his son’s death, making it difficult for him to return to India.

Following the issue, Bheemunipatnam MLA Ganta Srinivasa Rao took up the matter with Special Commissioner of the Andhra Pradesh Bhavan in New Delhi. Mr. Ganta also sought assistance in coordinating with the Indian Embassy representatives to facilitate Mr. Rao’s return to Visakhapatnam.

After reaching the city, Mr. Bhaskar Rao said the efforts of the MLA helped him return to Visakhapatnam and enabled him to see his son for the last time.

Surya Prakash was among the boys who were swept away by strong waves while playing in the sea near the IT SEZ Junction in Visakhapatnam on Friday. His death left the family devastated, and raised concerns about the safety of youngsters visiting the beach.

World.title: 'We are not yes-men': CM Afridi launches PTI long march to Islamabad, convoy enters Karak district
World.content:
PESHAWAR/LAKKI MARWAT/DI KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday launched the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad from Lakki Marwat, saying the party would “not accept” any policy that was against the interests of the people of KP.

The PTI has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government, which has vowed to prevent any violent gatherings in the capital. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan.

By late Sunday night, the convoy led by the KP chief minister had entered Karak district and reached Hamidan Chowk.

In a post shortly before 11pm, PTI said Afridi’s convoy was en route to Karak after the KP CM addressed supporters at a roundabout located at the border between Bannu and Karak districts.

Earlier in the day, Afridi reached Lakki Marwat by helicopter to lead his party’s long march, which was launched from Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Indus Highway.

In Lakki Marwat, an AFP journalist saw thousands of people take to the streets. Many of the demonstrators carried red and green flags of the PTI, and a huge billboard affixed on the side of a truck read “release Imran Khan” and featured a picture of the beaming former prime minister.

Addressing thousands of participants in Lakki Marwat, Afridi urged the public to step out of their homes for the sake of Pakistan, saying Imran, along with his wife and sisters, was in prison and they should show the world that they were the “true owners” of the country.

He said the “PTI’s negotiating committee had gone to Islamabad to lower the political temperature, but those making decisions behind closed doors had sabotaged the talks.

“They wanted their will to prevail in KP, but I declared that only Imran Khan’s vision and policies would be implemented here. We do not accept any policy that is not in the interest of the people of KP and the Pashtuns,” he maintained.

The chief minister declared: “We are not ‘yes-men’; we are soldiers of Imran Khan, and we will carry forward his policies.”

He repeatedly asked the crowd whether it supported a military operation, asking those opposed to it to raise their hands.

He questioned the policy being followed to tackle terrorism, saying: “What kind of policy is this, where terrorism has persisted for 22 years?”

KP CM insisted there had been peace during Imran’s government because his policies were sound, but following the “regime change operation”, terrorists were resettled, leading to “infinite terrorism”.

In 2023, after his ouster, Imran had defended his government’s plan to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

“We will eradicate terrorism, and if our policy is implemented, we will restore peace within 100 days,” he claimed.

He said the long march was being launched from Gandi Chowk and would conclude at another chowk. At this, the crowd shouted: “D-Chowk.”

“We are a political force and a party, and those who dream of the demise of the PTI can never succeed,” he added.

Afridi said the participants would leave from Gandi Chowk and their next stop would be Karak.

PTI workers had started gathering at Gandi Chowk on the Peshawar-Karachi Highway on Sunday afternoon to participate in the long march. Strict security measures were in place, with a large police contingent deployed at the site along with armoured personnel carriers and bomb disposal squads.

Afridi assailed for using ‘state helicopter’

A special helipad was prepared near Maidadkhel for Afridi and a video shared on social media platforms earlier showed a crowd of PTI workers gathered around it as KP’s chief executive touched down.

A video shared by the PTI on its X account showed Afridi’s convoy surrounded by a large crowd of party workers and supporters.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar criticised Afridi for using a “state helicopter for a political march”.

Calling the use of the helicopter a “violation of the Islamabad High Court’s orders”, he wrote on X, referring to a recent ruling that directed provincial governments to ensure that no government resources or machinery was used to facilitate any march or gathering.

“Terrorism is spreading in the province and Nero is playing his flute,” Tarar quipped.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said the use of the helicopter amounted to contempt of court by violating the IHC order.

“When the chief minister himself does not uphold the court’s orders and uses state resources for political activities, what expectation can there be for his workers to abide by the law?” Kundi wrote on X.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also made a sarcastic post on X, sharing the video and saying, “Sohail Afridi sahib’s Heli ride today from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat must have been for official work, possibly related to the security situation and counterterrorism efforts.”

Special Assistant to the KP CM for Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saad earlier told journalists at his residence that convoys from the southern KP districts would join the “peaceful long” march at Gandi Chowk.

“If workers from some southern districts, especially Tank and Waziristan, could not attend the long march today due to law and order-related curfew and other restrictions, they would join the movement on the way to Peshawar the next day,” he said.

Gandapur convoy returns to DI Khan

Earlier, PTI workers and supporters, led by former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, set out from Dera Ismail Khan to join the party’s long march at Lakki Marwat.

However, according to Gandapur, they were forced to return from Yarik on their way because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation.

The former KP CM insisted that the decision was taken to avoid exposing party workers to unnecessary risk, after the convoy remained stranded at Yarik for several hours.

Addressing the workers at Yarik, Gandapur noted that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days and that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation.

Gandapur told the workers that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision based on the prevailing circumstances, the safety of the workers and the instructions of the party leadership.

He said the workers could again set out to join the long march if the situation improved or the party leadership issued fresh instructions. The PTI leader contended that if the party leadership called him again, he could reach the long march within two hours.

He emphasised that the law and order situation did not warrant keeping a large number of workers at the site overnight.

The former KP CM also told the workers that they could remain at Yarik if they wanted to, but he could not violate the instructions issued by the party leadership.

He stressed that the decision taken by the senior leadership was not merely a personal decision, but one that he regarded as being in line with Imran’s instructions.

However, during the address, some workers expressed disagreement with the decision to take the convoy back. They said they wanted to remain at Yarik and continue their participation in the protest for as long as the movement continued.

Gandapur expressed displeasure over their position and urged them to take the practical situation on the ground into account. “TikTok-type talk” should not be made here, he told the workers, stressing that decisions had to be based on the situation on the ground.

The former KP CM subsequently persuaded the workers to return, following which the convoy left Yarik for DI Khan.

Before departing from DI Khan, the ex-CM stressed that the protest should remain peaceful and urged the participants to maintain discipline and refrain from violence, vandalism and confrontation with law enforcement personnel.

He said the party would follow a policy of “live and let live” during the protest and directed workers not to take the law into their hands.

“Those who block roads or engage in confrontation are not our workers,” Gandapur said, asking the participants to remain peaceful throughout the march.

He further urged the participants to avoid any activity that could lead to clashes or damage to public or private property.

The PTI’s march, being carried out to demand the release of its jailed founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan, is the latest bone of contention between the two sides.

In August, the PTI announced the long march to Islamabad on Sept 27 against what it called the “illegal imprisonment” of its party founder. However, a couple of days before its scheduled long march, the party postponed the march until Oct 4 (today).

Federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no option but to impose governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, citing the province’s security situation and the protest call, while PTI has warned of dire consequences if such a step was taken.

After weekend talks, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah has further warned that the protesters will not be allowed to enter Islamabad.

Plan for the march

According to the plan for the march shared by the KP CM on X, PTI supporters from the districts of Tank, Dera Ismail Khan, South Waziristan, North Waziristan and Bannu will join the long march from Lakki Marwat’s Gandi Chowk on Oct 4.

The caravan will halt for the night near Karak, from where people will depart at 12:30pm the next day and stay overnight near Kohat.

Then, at 12pm on Oct 6, protesters from Kohat, Hangu, Kurram, and Orakzai will join the convoy, which will move towards Peshawar and spend the night near Mattani.

The caravan will depart from Budh Bair in Peshawar on Oct 7 afternoon. “The remaining constituencies of Peshawar will join us at Kohat Road Bridge and the Motorway Toll Plaza. And we will spend the night near Charsadda Interchange,” the KP CM said.

They would then depart the Charsadda Interchange at 12:30pm on Oct 8 after people from Charsadda and Mohmand join them.

Refraining from detailing the final leg of the trip to the federal capital, Afridi said the people “of entire KP” would gather at Khairabad on Oct 8 and spend the night there. “God willing, the plan for the next phase will be announced there.”

Ahead of the march, movement on several roads on KP has been banned under Section 144.

Section 144 imposed in several KP districts

Section 144 has been imposed in several districts of KP through notifications issued by the respective deputy commissioners, with restrictions on the movement of people and vehicles along specified routes, citing security and public safety concerns.

In DI Khan, the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on specified roads and routes has been banned between 6am and 6pm from Oct 4 to Oct 6, citing the prevailing law-and-order situation and public safety concerns.

In Upper South Waziristan, Section 144 has been imposed from Oct 3 to Oct 5, banning the movement of cargo vehicles, rickshaws and dumpers over a possible VBSB/VBIED threat in adjoining areas.

In Lower South Waziristan, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 1 to Oct 10, banning the movement of loader rickshaws, single- and double-cabin cargo vehicles, Shahzore vehicles, Mazdas, Suzuki loaders and dumpers in Wana and Azam Warsak. The notification cited security and public safety concerns.

In District Tank, restrictions on the movement of individuals and all types of traffic along specified routes have been imposed under Section 144 from 9pm on Oct 3 until noon on Oct 5. The notification cited the prevailing law-and-order situation, public safety concerns and the need to ensure the safe movement of law enforcement personnel.

In Hangu, restrictions have been imposed under Section 144 from Oct 3 to Oct 6, banning the movement of individuals and all types of traffic on six routes, including the Hangu-Kohat, Hangu-Thall, Hangu Bypass and Hangu-Sumari roads.

The restrictions do not apply to law enforcement agencies and emergency services, while exemptions may be granted by the district police officer or security forces.

World.title: PTI terms access to Imran 'principal point of deadlock', claims Centre refused to include it in agreement
World.content:
The PTI on Sunday asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of its talks with the Centre was that the latter refused to incorporate terms regarding access to incarcerated party founder Imran Khan into a proposed agreement.

Hours-long negotiations yesterday between an opposition delegation comprising the PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP, ended in a deadlock.

While the federal government blamed the PTI for the failure of negotiations, the main opposition party denied the allegations and claimed that the federal government was responsible for all that happened on Saturday night.

In a press release posted on social media, the PTI expressed regret that the negotiations concluded without substantive progress, despite “serious efforts” to address concerns including political instability, access to the PTI founder as well as his medical treatment, and the worsening security situation in the country, particularly Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The statement said that the “principal point of the deadlock” was the party’s demand for immediate access to Imran, so that its leadership could consult him on matters of “national and political importance”.

According to the statement, the government agreed to restore meetings between Imran and his family members and lawyers from Tuesday, but did not agree to the additional measures concerning his medical assessment and treatment.

“In an effort to facilitate progress, the negotiating team conveyed that other demands could be set aside if the government agreed to this single request. However, according to PTI, the government declined to make access to Imran Khan part of the proposed agreement,” the PTI said.

“PTI welcomed the resumption of family and legal meetings but stressed that such access cannot substitute for proper medical examination and necessary treatment,” the statement read, adding that the party called for Imran’s health to be addressed with “seriousness, transparency and humanitarian consideration”.

The party stressed that just as leaders of other political parties remained central to decision-making and policy, the PTI must also be allowed to consult its chairman; restricting such consultation limited the scope for meaningful political engagement, it added.

Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023, for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

Despite an order by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) allowing him twice-a-week meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays with his family, lawyers and other associates, Imran has been restricted from meeting visitors for several months.

His health has deteriorated over the course of his prison sentence, prompting outcry from members of the party.

According to the PTI, Imran’s health and medical treatment were also raised as a matter of fundamental importance in the talks, with the negotiating team seeking immediate access to him, his transfer to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for treatment, and the constitution of an “appropriate” medical board — including his personal physician — to ensure his proper examination, diagnosis and treatment.

After his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January, Imran has been provided with treatment at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

In mid-August, the Supreme Court ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment. However, the government later revealed that Imran was instead taken to Pims, prompting a strong reaction from his family and party.

Security situation in KP

The security situation in KP also featured prominently in the discussions, with the PTI saying it stressed that the concerns of the public must remain central to counterterrorism policies.

According to the statement, the Centre sought the provincial government’s “unconditional support” for its counterterrorism measures and operations as well as support for imposing emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged districts and adjoining areas.

“The PTI reiterated its unequivocal condemnation of terrorism and stressed that eliminating terrorism, protecting citizens and restoring lasting peace must remain a national priority,” it said, adding that the party paid tribute to the officers and personnel of the authorities that have sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism and expressed solidarity with civilians and families who had suffered from terrorist violence.

“Terrorism cannot be defeated through force alone or through unilateral measures that could expose innocent civilians to further loss of life, property or displacement,” the party maintained, calling for a strategy that combined “firm action against terrorism with protection of civilian populations and sensitivity to local realities”.

Accordingly, it proposed a meeting within 72 hours of authorised representatives of the federal and provincial governments to develop a mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism. It also proposed consultation with political parties represented in the KP Assembly, elected representatives, tribal elders and other relevant stakeholders in order for the policy to enjoy public confidence and be implemented effectively.

PTI also rejected attempts to characterise the position of KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as political obstinacy, arguing that “had access to Imran Khan been facilitated, the chief minister could have consulted the PTI chairman directly on security and counterterrorism policy, potentially helping to bridge differences and create greater consensus”.

Responding to the press conference held by federal ministers after the talks ended without result, PTI said the government should address the substantive issues that prevented progress instead of seeking to place the responsibility on the opposition.

It called for an explanation as to why immediate access to Imran was considered unacceptable, why requests regarding his medical care were not accommodated, and why the proposed broader consultative approach was not accepted for developing a sustainable security strategy in KP.

The party reiterated that it remains “prepared to engage in political dialogue, constitutional processes, meaningful consultation and national consensus to address Imran Khan’s health and treatment, restoration of democracy, supremacy of the Constitution and law, political stability, terrorism and the wider challenges confronting Pakistan”.

The party stressed, however, that “meaningful negotiations” could not succeed through predetermined positions or demands for unconditional endorsement.

“Serious dialogue requires flexibility, mutual confidence, consultation and a genuine willingness to translate discussions into practical progress,” the statement added.

‘Three fundamental red lines’

Separately, Opposition Chief Whip Malik Aamir Dogar stated that the talks had fallen through on “three fundamental red lines”: meetings with Imran, his medical treatment, and KP’s terrorism policy.

“We made it clear that the authority to call off the long march rests solely with Imran Khan sahib, so a meeting with him is essential,” he said in a post on X.

The MNA added that, when the government was unwilling to do this, an alternative demand for Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas’s meeting with Imran was also put forward, but similarly rejected.

On the PTI founder’s health, Dogar said that the opposition’s minimum demand had been the inclusion of his personal physicians in his treatment to dispel “doubts and suspicions” about his health. This, too, was not agreed to, which heightened the opposition’s concerns.

The third “red line”, he said, was that the opposition demanded that “no decision be made unilaterally” regarding KP’s security and terrorism policy, but rather that all relevant stakeholders be taken into confidence.

“Instead of broad consultations on this matter, the government sought hasty decisions within 72 hours,” he said.

As a result of the government’s refusal of these demands and the party’s refusal to back down from them, he added, the negotiations ended in a deadlock.

Salman Akram notes Centre’s ‘insistence on unilateral’ CT measures

Earlier, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja asserted that the main reason for the breakdown of talks with the Centre was the latter’s insistence on “unilateral” counter-terrorism measures in KP.

In a post on X, Raja wrote that the “primary reason for the failure of the talks around 3am this morning” was that the “PTI-TTAP team stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions in KPK would be based on agreement between the federal government and the KPK government”.

He said the opposition wanted those actions to be “framed on the basis of consultation with, and the buy-in of, the different political parties represented” in the KP Assembly.

“This was not acceptable to the government team, that insisted that all actions unilaterally initiated by it would have to be owned by the provincial government,” Raja asserted.

“The PTI-TTAP team was clear that we have zero tolerance for terrorism and are committed to rooting it out. We also have a clear position against so-called collateral damage in the form of innocent lives and internal displacement of the local population.”

Raja noted that counterterrorism policies require support from the local population and ground intelligence.

“The wisdom provided by the jirga held in the KP assembly of all the political and tribal notables of the province, including the merged districts, must be heeded.

“This was not acceptable to the federal government,” he wrote.

In November last year, a peace jirga held at the KP Assembly, also attended by the governor, demanded that the Centre consult the KP government over Afghan policy.

Tarar accuses KP govt of ‘supporting’ terrorism

On the other hand, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar responded to Raja in a lengthy post on X, questioning why the KP government has not taken action against terrorism.

“It is only now, when your KP government is politically weak, [that] you have started responding to the federal government’s calls for [a] joint mechanism to fight terrorism, that too only as a strategy to save your political capital in KP,” the minister alleged.

“This is an old strategy of PTI, that when under pressure, they start talking of consultations and joint actions, but on [the] ground they do the exact opposite.”

Accusing the KP government of “double standards and hypocrisy”, Tarar contended that while it said it was taking steps to fight terrorism, its “narrative on terrorism is in favour of terrorists”.

“KPK government’s policy only encourages and supports [the] spread of terrorism in the province,” the PML-N leader alleged.

Tarar questioned why the KP government had not taken steps against terrorism or convened the provincial apex committee for meetings and why it had not condemned the “TTA regime for sponsoring terrorism inside Pakistan and conduct of cross-border attacks on the posts and drone attacks by them”.

“Why hasn’t the KPK Government not implemented NAP as per which clear action is required against illegal spectrum, illegal Afghan immigrants, measures for capacity enhancement of Police and [Counter-Terrorism Department]?” he added.

He asked why PTI leaders did not visit checkposts of security forces and police to express their support, and whether they had taken interest in the governance and development of esrtwhile Fata.

The minister urged the PTI to “stop selling this false narrative of collective consultations, jirgas or any other method, as this means nothing on [the] ground other than delaying tactics”.

Tarar reiterated his comments in a televised video statement, slamming the PTI for failing to abandon “double standards and hypocrisy”, which he said resulted in deadly terrorist attacks in KP.

“We were considering that they may go back on their word, and I had been saying it for the past two and a half weeks: if we are going to talk, then who should we talk to? And if we talk, what guarantee do we have that they will honour their word?” the minister asked.

He accused the PTI of taking U-turns and “expressing pride in them”, as well as failing to maintain a steady stance on the issue of protecting the lives and property of KP’s residents.

“Now different statements are emerging: Salman Akram Raja is saying one thing; [Adviser to KP Chief Minister on Information] Shafi Jan is saying that they want to change the policy on terrorism,” he added. “What is your policy? Does it even exist?”

Tarar alleged: “The only policy you have is deliberately supporting terrorism. Your policy is how you can elevate terrorists, how you can build a political terror-crime nexus and how you can spread terrorism across the province.

“I said earlier that you have to decide whether you stand with Pakistan or Afghanistan. You take the benefits of Pakistan, but are in favour of Afghanistan.”

“The policy change they are talking about is to give terrorists cover and protection,” Tarar further claimed.

He said people of KP were being killed in terrorist incidents because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi “wants to free one prisoner”.

“Lives have been wasted and people have been martyred because the province’s CM prioritises the release of one convicted prisoner,” he insisted. “This is why I say they (PTI) are TTP’s (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) B-team and TTA’s (Afghan Taliban) C-team,” the PML-N leader alleged.

The minister further accused the KP government of having a “pro-terrorism mindset”, which he contended had contributed to a failure to prevent terrorist attacks and cross-border firing from Afghanistan.
